## The rules established on the page in this batch, which Volume 04 must then keep

1. **A review is a day a person comes to, and it is not a hearing.** There is nobody to hear anything: no assessor, no chair, no minute, no form. The only question on the sheet is whether a person is in the room, and the only evidence there is a mark in a column in a book, made by somebody who was not the person who came. **A reader who is paid can be told to stop, and a person whose attendance is recorded by a third person is a person whose attendance can be recorded wrongly by a third person, and there is no column anywhere on that bank for a person who turns up on the second day and says it was not the first.**
2. **A date is a piece of paper and it has to be carried, and the person who carries it is not paid to carry it.** A court will not fix it, because a list of works is not an instrument and there is nothing to file and a form came back with a reason in it and no box for a why. A seat will not pay it, because the district's flood authority was given to two persons and the second of them refused it in nine words, and an office that has disclaimed the power to compel work has no money and no fund and no line, and the Company's whole money is four shillings a year and all of it is the rent of a building. **A date that is not carried is a date that does not exist, and there is no office in this empire whose job it is to know whether a review happened.**
3. **A review a person has to walk to is a review of the people who can walk.** The price of one is not money: it is four shillings a year of rent, one reader's wage for two days, the walking that is not that wage, about four people who cannot read a paragraph and were never asked, about nine more who cannot read one, about nine who said yes and did not come, and one bench that will not take a woman of sixty-four. **Not one of those lines is a line anybody can be given money for, and the two lines that could be are the two lines there are.**
4. **There is one cart on that bank and it belongs to a man who is on the list, and a man who is on the list has to come to the day as a person coming and not as the man bringing the cart, and if he brings the cart he is working and not attending, and if he does not, about eleven people do not come.** Nobody had thought of it and it took a woman of twenty-eight about nine minutes.
5. **Every record on that bank is a person, and a person is not a record, and a person can be told to stop, and a slate can be washed, and a book in a hired store can lose its building, and a satchel can go into a house and stay there.** Four objects on a bench and no fifth one in this empire that any of them can hold. **And a slate washed on purpose by a named person on a named day is a record and a slate washed by accident is a piece of chalk.**
6. **A duty is found to have stopped when somebody stands in a room and does not do it, and that is the only instrument in this empire that can stop a duty.** A no with a reason in it is in a book; a no with no reason in it is in a doorway; the reason the nineteen said no with a reason is that somebody held a book and said *say the reason and I will write it*, and the reason about four were never asked is that nobody stood in front of them with a sheet. **About four duties have not been shown to have stopped and have not been shown to have started, and there is no column for either.**
7. **A season that nobody has agreed to is not a season.** The first was agreed to by about forty-one people who said yes with a day against them and a day against the day they were asked. It ended by arithmetic, because ninety days from the second of the fifth month of next year is a day and not a notice. **Arithmetic is not a notice, and the notice on the reader's engagement is the same notice as everybody else's and has no second season in it and no date at the end of anything at all, and a date at the beginning of a thing is not a date at the end of it.**
8. **A person must not be put in a list to explain a cost to a room.** The girl of seventeen walked up a lane with a slate to go to four doors, got to the second one, and did not knock, and gave the reason: **they have not been asked once, and asking them now would mean a day against a name in about four years, and the person who wrote the day would be a girl of seventeen who is paid forty-five pence a day to read and was not paid to come up that lane.** And: **the machine works by somebody standing in front of another person with a sheet. It does not work by a person being written down after the fact.**
9. **The answer to the question bought at a shilling in the second week of the fifth month of next year is a row and not a leaf.** The row records a striking-out; a striking-out of a leaf out of a bound schedule is done with an impression, because an impression is the only thing in that building that will take a number, and a run number is how that office accounts for a thing it did not make. **A bound schedule does not travel.** It is in the fourth press, in a wall, in a corridor behind a court on a flood terrace, and it has been in that corridor longer than anybody in that building has been alive.
10. **A copy of a thing is a fact about the copying, and the copying is not the thing.** A copy may be had for fourpence out of a press at a counter in a city. **A leaf of a bound schedule may not be taken out by anybody: the binding is what holds the schedule whole, and a leaf out of a bound schedule is a removal, and a removal is a different sentence from a gap, and a gap in a copy is a fact about the copying.** The two sentences are kept apart on the page and are both said by a person and not by a narrator.
11. **Three things are required — a written application, a court direction, a recorded custody entry — and one is had.** A court direction is a direction of a court, and a notary's table is not a court, and a clerk of thirty-four looked for a form for asking a court for anything for about nine minutes and is telling the size of the looking.
12. **A recorded custody entry is not a thing a court grants and not a thing a form produces. It is a thing a person writes down**, in four lines: the thing, the person in charge of it, the day it was taken, and the signature of the person who took it. **There is no line on the form for a body, and that is not a design decision, that is a fact about bodies, and the form has carried that fact for a hundred and forty years without printing it, and the reason nobody has printed it is that a body has never once been able to answer for itself and everybody who has used that form has known it without being told.**
13. **A person in charge of a bound schedule in a press is a person, and a press is not a person, and a person cannot be appointed to it by anybody who is not standing in the corridor. If a thing has been in a press for a hundred and forty years and nobody has ever been put in charge of it then there is no entry, and there never has been one, and the absence is not a gap. The absence is the record.**
14. **A custody entry is a statement that somebody was in the room, and the whole of what it requires is a person who can be instructed and who can stop. That is why a door has to be opened by a person and not by a body, and it is not strength and it is not law.**
15. **A thing that depends on a person can be taken away by the person stopping, and a duty that stops is not a duty that survives stopping, and a person cannot be compelled to be in a room and there is no form in this empire for it.** And the positive form, in a clerk's mouth: **a person who is going to be asked to stand in a room ought to be told how long she has, and nobody in this matter has told anybody how long they have.**
16. **A person in charge of a thing is not a party to it, and it is the only position in this matter that is not a party.** A party is a person a book can be true about and can be served; the person in charge of a press is a person a book can be true about and is served, and is asked, and holds no box and no sheet and no fee and no term and no day at the end of it. **There is no form that makes a person be in charge of a thing, there never has been, and the way the clerk came by it is that she was the only one left holding a key.** And it is the only one of the four positions in this matter that anybody can stop.
17. **A party is served and a witness is asked, and a person cannot be both in the same room about the same thing, and that is not a rule anybody made, it is what the two words mean.** Which means the two people who asked a question are the two people who cannot witness what is done in answer to it, and the witness has to be somebody who has come to a window about something else. **And being a witness does not mean being to blame for anything; it means that in about four years there is one person who can say they were standing in a corridor.**
18. **A roll is a copy of a copy of a thing, and every copy in it is a person copying, and a person can be put into a column of a roll by hand and a person can be taken out of it by hand, and there is nothing in this empire that stops anybody doing it, and that is not a flaw in the record — that is what a record is, and it is the reason nobody has ever been able to find out who did a particular one: not because it was well done, because it was ordinary.** And it will be exactly as true in nine years.
19. **A person who corrects a roll and leaves nothing is not cautious, she is invisible, and an invisible correction is a correction that can be attributed to anybody.** So a correction carries the corrector's name and the day, and the corrector's hand can be compared against her hand for forty years. **That is a cost of the method and not only a protection, and it is the same document in both readings.**
20. **A provincial archivist who answers a stranger's question about a roll is a provincial archivist who has put a stranger's question into a roll, and there is no form anywhere for taking a question back out of a record.** There is one for taking a person's name out of a box at a notary's table and none at all for taking a question out of a page, and the looking took nine years.
21. **A list of works with a person's name at the foot of it is the only kind of sentence in this empire that a person can act on the same day, and it is that because a foreman nails it to a rail at a gate and anybody may come and read it. Take the name off and it is a list of jobs with nobody's promise at the end of it, and a list of jobs with nobody's promise at the end of it does not stop. It goes on.**
22. **A schedule of a term is a list of holders and days, and a line with no day on the end of it is an office that has been made to go on by a person, and the person who took the day out of it had to have hands.** And the harder half: **there is no column in that book for the person who emptied the line, because a schedule of a term is not a register of duties, and a great many people have believed those two books were the same one, and they are not.**
23. **A refusal that is anticipated is a threat and a refusal that is applied for is a document.** Being right is what makes a document, a document is findable, and there is no way in this empire to un-ask. **And a refusal is not a denial and is not a confirmation, and it is a document about a person who would not say a word, and everybody entitled to read into it whatever they had already decided to read into it is doing so entirely correctly and it is their business and not his.**
24. **The rule of the twelfth month of last year does not apply to a day.** Used once in this batch, in writing with a date, and answered in a room in words with a date, and the answer is that a rule that only ever works in one direction is not a rule, it is a preference. **This is the third correct non-use anybody has made with it.**

## The calendar of this batch, as printed

**The batch runs from the first week of the eighth month of next year to the last week of the tenth month of next year, which is where Chapter 0160 left off.** Ch 161 the first week of the eighth, the review, on the bank; Ch 162 the first week into the second week of the eighth, the cost of attendance; Ch 163 the first week of the eighth in Auremar, the answer at the counter, **the same week as Chapter 0161 and not a coincidence anybody arranged**; Ch 164 the second week into the third week of the eighth, the first fortnight of a season nobody agreed to; Ch 165 the third week of the eighth into the first week of the ninth, the road down; Ch 166 the second week of the ninth, at a lock; Ch 167 the third week into the fourth week of the ninth, a back room on a flood terrace; Ch 168 the first week of the tenth, a clerk's window and a corridor; Ch 169 the second week into the third week of the tenth, the press and the direction; Ch 170 the last week of the tenth, the notice on a nail and the plainest words.

**Five journeys and five completed, thirty days.** Up in the first week of the fifth month of next year, down in the last week of it, up in the third week of the seventh, **and the fifth journey in this batch: down the old river road from the third week of the eighth into the first week of the ninth, arriving on the Slade on the second day of the first week of the ninth, and a lock on the same road in the second week of the ninth.** A day of a wage of seventeen shillings and a penny the week is a little over two shillings and fivepence; six days is a little over fourteen shillings; **twenty-one days is two pounds and eleven shillings and threepence, twenty-four days is about three pounds, and thirty days is three pounds and thirteen shillings and threepence out of about forty-four pounds a year, and there is no fund and there is no form for a fund.**

**Inherited dates spent or named in this batch, none of them moved.** The first season began on the second of the fifth month of next year and is about ninety days, and **its review is about the first week of the eighth month of next year and this batch spends it.** The question was bought in the second week of the fifth month of next year at a shilling and **its answer is due in the first week of the eighth month of next year and this batch spends it.** The reader's engagement is **not printed in this batch at all and no elapsed period is computed from it anywhere.** The first exception's withdrawal document, dated the twenty-fourth of the ninth month of last year and effective the second of the fifth month of next year, is **not printed.** The first door-to-door asking, the seventh of the seventh month, and the day a chair was fixed, the fifteenth of it, are **not printed.** The Sorn enrolment of the eighth of the seventh month is **not printed.** The rule of the twelfth month of last year is **named once, in Chapter 0170**, and used with a date.

**And one date this batch is forbidden to have, and does not have.** No chapter prints a date, an age, or a number of years for the arrangement that made the Kest record unusable, for the redaction, for the rows in the register, or for the woman who arranged it, and no chapter says how long ago anything in the Kest file happened, and **no chapter says that the woman called Kest is Ilyra Kest.** A retired scale notary of sixty-one or two appears on a towpath in Chapter 0166 and refuses a first name, and the refusal is a refusal to confirm and not a denial, and **the page nowhere turns it into an assertion and no character treats it as one.** This is Batch 0001's second proposed canon change, inherited and carried and not re-argued.

## The figures this batch printed, and which of them are new

**Inherited and unmoved, and every one verified on the page of this batch or carried as a fact:** a shilling for a question at a notary's table; fourpence for a copy; about eleven weeks for an answer; ninepence for a carrier at a lock; **about four hundred forms in a box under the fourth counter, and the box's counts — two hundred and sixty-one empty, a hundred and forty filled, fourteen with a body in the box, eleven with a person's name and a date underneath in a different hand — are not printed in this batch and are not altered**; a hundred and forty years at that practice; **forty-five pence a day for the reader, four days a week, on a written engagement with a copy in a satchel and the same notice as everybody else; a reader's day is between four pence and a shilling; seventeen shillings and a penny the week; three pounds and thirteen shillings and threepence; one shilling and sixpence a day for a barrow of stone, a man and a boy, ninety days being a hundred and thirty-five shillings, which is six pounds fifteen shillings; four shillings a year, all of it the rent of a hired stone store; about nine men in three gangs, one of whom has said out loud that asking may have cost him the contract; a factor of forty-six unanswered; about nineteen pounds three and fourpence at Lowcross, unpaid, nobody liable, no line for a bridge in that fund in nineteen years, about a penny a day, four hundred and eleven on the far side, three hundred and eighty-eight crossings; about four hundred and forty foot of outer face; eleven feet high; a hundred and forty yards below the ford; the north bay about thirty-one foot by nineteen and about thirty people; a bench about two feet higher than the bench in the middle; about a hundred and forty feet of ditch on the south side and a scour at the third-of-the-way place; about nine hundred and forty names in nine hands with about four hundred of them dead; about two hundred and forty people who have never known the sixth space is there; about four hundred and thirty miles each way and about six days; a lock a hundred and forty yards below a landing; a clerk's window about four feet off the ground and about two feet wide; a court room, a back room and four presses in an embankment corridor; nine completed terms in a bound schedule and a tenth with a holder and no day; a hall about thirty feet long.** The **fifth heading of the register of pending duties is *Copy sold*** and is printed once, in Chapter 0168, and the **fourth column reads *next review: none named*** and is printed once, in the same chapter, without a count.

**New figures established on the page in this batch, and available to the rest of the volume.** **About thirty-one people came to the first review, of about forty-one who said yes, and about nine of the forty-one did not come, and nobody on that bank knows which nine.** A court's window that is a door with a counter in front of it, and a press that is a door, and a bay's west door that is a door, and **no form anywhere that joins any of them.** A form for a recorded custody entry with four lines on it, written out in a hand of about sixty off a memory of about sixty years, **and no fifth line, and no line for a body.** A district court's reason for refusing a direction, in a form, in four days, **and the word *bound* in the middle of it with about nine words on either side.** A provincial record office's ordinary round of eleven stops, **ten of them buildings and one a man in a house, and a man in a house is the only stop on that card anybody can turn her away from, and eight of the other ten are rooms with a person in charge who cannot say no to the person who lifts.** Nine lines in a margin in nine counties in nine years. And **the first time in nine years that a man of fifty at a clerk's window has been asked a question and has said the whole of it out loud: *I did not think of it like that.***

## The locks, checked over the ten files, and how

Every one of these was searched over `chapters/volume-04/chapter-016[1-9].md` and `chapter-0170.md` and held, and the method is given because the Volume 03 audit's own method note is that a claim of absence is cheap and a claim of uniqueness is the one that costs.

- **Calendar month names and weekday names.** `grep -rniE "\b(january|february|march|april|may|june|july|august|september|october|november|monday|tuesday|wednesday|thursday|friday|saturday|sunday)\b"` over the ten files returns **ten lines, and every one of the ten is the modal verb *may*.** **No calendar month name and no weekday name appears anywhere in the batch.** No weekday name was written and corrected, because none was written.
- **The substituted phrase *the present holder*: absent. The word *exception*: absent, and there is no Stage 2 instrument in the batch, so the word has nothing to be used of. The word *precedent*: absent. The word *certification*: absent.** The two documents, the quarterly return, Hallis Dren's return of the eleventh of the tenth, the substituted wording, the public-necessity sentence, the three red things, the two sealed pages, the counting-house mark, the year in the run, forty-four thousand eight hundred and nineteen, the ninety-second leaf, the word *eligibility*, and any name of the Ashfall bundle or of Ilyra Kest: **every one of them is absent, and no chapter refers to what Ilyra Kest found as a question.**
- **The three Orises: none of the three is named. Oren Tal is in the batch and is not asked to explain himself, and the fourth hour of Chapter 0166 is the not-asking. Aurelia Pell is in the batch and is a separate person from her father; the two are in the same river district on the same day and neither has looked for the other, and the same surname is not a door into anything and is not used as one.**
- **Pell Vey: not on the page at all.** His hand and the column headed *by whose authority* are referred to in Chapter 0163 and the name in that column is **not read out anywhere in the batch**, and about thirty rows in that run that are not instruments are referred to and not developed, and the documentation of that hand is the volume's last two batches.
- **The Venn ruling is never said to have four terms.** The fourth term and the fifth term are named in Chapter 0164 and the fifth term is the district works, a list of works. The schedule on the rail is referred to in Chapter 0164 **without a date and without a figure of an age**, with the four old nails and the four new nails, and nobody pulls anything down. **The date that schedule went on the rail is printed nowhere in this batch and its age is not restated.**
- **The three thirty-ones and the two other pattern-figures.** The thirty-one of Mosswake is not in this batch and is not referred to as a debt of it. **The batch's own about thirty-one at the review is a fifth thirty-one and is in Chapters 0161, 0163 and 0170, and no sentence in the batch sets it beside the thirty-one households behind the bank or the about thirty-one people in a lane at the north of the ford, and the passage that carries it gives about forty-one and about thirty-one together as two counts of one question.** The guild's hundred and thirty-five shillings is not in this batch. The Company's about nine hundred and forty names and the about two hundred and forty people who have never known the sixth space is there are in one sentence in Chapter 0167 and neither is set beside the about nine hundred blanks a year of a rack, which is not in the batch at all. **The box under the fourth counter holds forms and is not mentioned; no count of forms, blanks or people leaves the page wrong.**
- **The guarantee: not paraphrased into a new order, not answered, not extended, and named three times, in Chapters 0161, 0164 and 0170, in the page's own inherited wording — offered at no charge, answerable at any time afterwards by a person answering in its terms, about sixty children under sixteen inside it. No child is named. The third instrument of Volume 03 is not withdrawn, varied, extended or disowned.**
- **The people on the bank are not devices.** The girl of eleven at the Reed Cut gate is read to in Chapter 0164 and is given no reason and is owed nothing. Bel Skell, about seventy-one, is asked at her own door four times a year as she asked in writing, **says the same reason for the second time, and is not asked a third time and is not going to be.** Rosamund Crane, eleven, who reads, is not the girl of eleven and is not in this batch. The boy of fifteen who cannot stand on the leg is in Chapter 0164, the ground was flat, somebody noticed, and **no chapter states that the leg is permanently injured.** Raff Ordway, sixteen, is on the list of works and **no chapter says how he got there.** The woman of about thirty-one at the first house appears twice, is a description and not a name, has not been asked for a name again, and **is not a symbol of anything.** **A reader of seventeen is a person and not a device.** Kem Ostry, thirty-one, is not named; the man of thirty-one with the cart in Chapter 0162 is reached as a description, as Batch 0001's decision requires.
- **The relationship: no romance begins and nothing on the page reads as intimacy in the ordinary sense.** The V3 half of the milestone is not re-paid and is not re-staged. **The paper that puts Tamsin Rook in his rooms and the watch that requires a person not from the office in his rooms are two instruments and are not merged in this batch**, and Chapter 0169 has her refuse a question about a corridor rather than a room and say the words *that is a fact and not advice* twice out loud to nobody. **The undertaking of the fourth of the first month is live, unretired, unamended and is not exercised.** **The fourth envelope in her drawer is mentioned once in the batch, in Chapter 0169, in a sentence that does not touch it: it is not opened, not sent, and it is the fourth time in two years she has not thought about it.**
- **No System panel appears in the batch and none is required.** The manuscript's system is intrinsic and has never been a panel. **The mark on the inside of his left wrist is not mentioned once in these ten chapters** and is not the price.
- **Card language in the narration.** A search of the ten files for *in this chapter, in this batch, on this page, this book, the reader of, it is recorded here, a hundred and sixty chapters* returned **five real sites and all five were rewritten as scenes or as narration before the batch closed**: a sentence in Chapter 0165 that said *the number the page has is twenty-four days*; a sentence in Chapter 0166 that called a refusal not-to-be-explained *a decision about the rest of this book*; a sentence in Chapter 0169 that said *it is recorded here that she said the words*, which is now a thing she says out loud to nobody in a corridor; a line in Chapter 0162 spoken by a character about writing a thing down; and a line in Chapter 0170 that said a fact *was on a page now*, which is now on the record in two places, in two cities, between two women who have never met.
- **The distances.** About four hundred and thirty miles each way and about six days and no chapter pretends it is shorter; a hundred and forty yards below the ford, twice; the north bay about thirty-one foot by nineteen; the tool shed about four hundred yards from the bay; a cart road on the far side of a lock. **There is no two hundred and forty yards anywhere in the batch** and the only two-hundred-and-forty figure used is about two hundred and forty people who have never known the sixth space is there. **Nothing in the batch places the hired store at a fixed distance from the ford.**

## The craft bounds, measured, and the method stated before the claim

The outline binds emphasis at about a fifth of a chapter's **lines** and about a fifth of a chapter's **prose text**, and requires a batch to say which of the two it measured and with what method. **Both were measured, over all ten files, and both hold.**

**On lines:** lines carrying a `**` over all lines, all-lines denominator. **Minimum 4.3% in Chapter 0169, maximum 14.8% in Chapter 0166, median 9.8%.** Ten of ten at or under a fifth. **This is the measure Volume 03 passes on, where the volume runs 2% to 22% with a median of 14%, and the batch's median is lower than the volume's.** The denominator is named because the review of Batch 0001 established that a lines figure is denominator-sensitive: on a non-blank-line denominator the same ten chapters of Batch 0001 ran 12.0% to 29.3%.

**On prose text:** characters inside `**…**` as a share of non-blockquote characters with the asterisks removed from the denominator, and with the asterisks paired inside the paragraph. **Minimum 10.7% in Chapter 0168, maximum 18.4% in Chapter 0164, median 17.2%.** Ten of ten at or under a fifth. **This is the measure Volume 03 fails on, where the volume runs 3% to 42% with a median of 23% and thirty-two of fifty chapters are over a fifth, and the batch's maximum is under the volume's median.** A batch that claimed only the lines measure would have been claiming the easy half.

**The first draft of the batch failed the text measure and the repair is part of the record.** The first pass ran 22.2% to 37.5% with a median of 30.1%, because the emphasis had been written as two, three and four-sentence runs opening a speech. **The repair was structural and not a deletion: every run of more than one sentence was cut back to its first sentence, and the sentences that followed were left in the chapter unemphasised, and the emphasis that survived is a sentence or a clause.** Ten of ten at or under a fifth on both measures afterwards. **And a chapter that is added to has to be re-measured, and all ten were re-measured, twice.**

**The pairing test, run because it is the one that produced a false baseline in Volume 03's own review.** A paragraph-level and blockquote-block-level parity test over all ten files, counting every paragraph and every blockquote block and never pairing across a blank line, **returns zero odd blocks.** One unpaired marker was found and fixed in Chapter 0169 before the test was run twice clean.

**No more than one emphasised clause in any one speech turn:** after the repair, the runs left standing are a clause or a single sentence, and a blockquoted form keeps its own typography and is not counted as a default.

**`about nine`, measured with `grep -o 'about nine' file | wc -l` per file and summed, which is the method the inherited figure was measured with and which counts *about nine hundred*, *about nine minutes* and *about nineteen*.** **Minimum 2 in Chapter 0165, maximum 8 in Chapters 0161 and 0170, median 7, ten of ten at or under the bound of about eight.** The thins were made by deleting a counted clause or referring to a thing instead of its number — *about nine people in front of her who cannot read a paragraph* became *people in front of her who cannot read a paragraph* — and **not by substituting a sibling figure: no figure the state files record verbatim was changed, and `about four`, `about forty`, `about thirty`, `about twenty`, `about sixty` and `about nineteen` were not swapped in for any of them.** The canon figure *about nine people cannot read a paragraph* is on the page three times and is the reason the bound was reached and not exceeded.

**`fourteen months` is zero times in the batch, and that is a decision and not an oversight.** The bound fixed in the review of Batch 0001 attaches the figure to one fact — the fourteen months in which Marek Kest and Tamsin Rook have been making names findable — and at most four in a chapter. **This batch had no occasion for that work: it is a batch about a day, a corridor and a press, and the two journeys of it that the figure would have fitted were written without it.** The first draft carried it four times, twice attached to a man having one day of his own wage in a week and twice attached to a book with no office on it, and **all four were cut by referring to the thing rather than to its length**, and no figure the state files record was changed to thin it. **A writer who needs a duration in this volume must use the thing's own duration, named from the page, and if the page has none, print none.**

**A duplicate audit, run over the ten files, returning zero.** Every paragraph longer than eighty characters and every sentence longer than seventy is counted across the batch: **no paragraph and no sentence occurs twice.** Three duplications were found by that audit and all three were rewritten before the batch closed: a reader asking a question out loud in Chapters 0161 and 0164, a finding about a duty and a room stated twice in Chapter 0164 and once in its own written form and again in Chapter 0165, and a sentence about a custody entry in Chapters 0166 and 0168. **In Chapter 0165 the second of the two ledger entries is now given in narration and not re-quoted, because a man reading a ledger aloud in a room and the reader of a chapter are two different acts and the chapter had been doing both.**

## The two proposed canon changes, carried and not acted on

1. **The date of the arrangement that made the Kest record unusable is still not reconcilable between the volume outline and the bible, and this batch has no date for it at all.** `outline/volume-04.md` and the phase prompt attach *about thirty-one years ago* to a retired scale notary being trained by a woman called Kest; `bible/characters.md` makes the arrangement an act of Ilyra Kest made twelve years before the opening case. **A man of sixty-one or two appears in Chapter 0166 on a towpath, gives a document, and refuses a first name, and the refusal is a refusal to confirm and is not a denial and is not a confirmation, and the page nowhere turns it into an assertion.** The winning card is still *print no date, no age, and no number of years for the arrangement, for the redaction, for the rows in the run, or for the woman*, and the page follows it. **The disagreement is not resolved by this batch and is not resolved by recording it.**
2. **The building is a *hired stone store* in this batch and is not called anything else anywhere in it, and nobody on the page is told which of the page's two names is right.** It is printed four times, in Chapters 0162 and 0165. **Neither measurement of the south end of it is printed and neither is used in an argument.** This is the fourth of the four items under the Volume 04 locks and it is a question and not a repair.

## What this batch owes the third batch, in one place

**A room to be cleared on the fourth**, on a notice that is a list of works with a district at the foot of it and no day at the end of it, and the person in charge of the press is the only person in this matter anybody can stop, and a person cannot be compelled to be in a room. **A bound schedule with nine completed terms and a tenth whose holder is the office and whose day has been taken out of a line that is otherwise there, and no column in that book for the person who emptied it.** **A copy of ten entries on four sheets in the inside of a coat, and no leaf out of the binding.** **A refusal in a form with a day on it, a name at the foot of it, no box for a why, and the word *bound* in the middle of the sentence.** **A first name refused at a lock on a towpath, entered, findable, and not a denial.** **A method given away for nothing by a woman who is not an ally: a person can be put into a column of a roll by hand and taken out by hand, and it will be exactly as true in nine years.** **A woman of twenty-eight who keeps a bay, who said the room is for the asking, and a carter of thirty-one who is on the list first and is owed a hearing and is not named.** **A reader of seventeen who has asked out loud, once on a platform and once in a bay, and who has not been answered, and who is not told that she is a party to anything.** **The second season, running, agreed to by nobody, asked of nobody.** **And nothing of the midpoint, and nothing of the Ashfall bundle, and nothing of what Ilyra Kest found.**

# THE REVIEW REPAIR OF VOLUME 04 BATCH 0002, CHAPTERS 161–170

**A review ran on the tenth batch's writer work (`logs/batch-0002.review.log`) and returned ten findings: six high, four medium, and a list of things it verified clean and told the next repair pass not to spend itself on. All six high findings and all four medium findings are fixed. No chapter was restarted, no plot was changed, no date moved, no canon figure altered, and no open thread was closed or opened. `git diff --numstat` over the batch is thirty-four insertions and thirty-six deletions across six chapter files, and the prompt is one line changed, and the manuscript moved from 616,477 words to 616,778.**

## The six high findings, and what each one was

1. **`chapter-0170.md:61` — one speech turn carried facts belonging to three speakers, and the batch's close turned on it.** The turn gave Marek Kest a rule he has not been using, a duration that is Tamsin Rook's, and *"a man I work with in a city four hundred and thirty miles up this river"* — a man who is not established anywhere, and who is Nevin Trost, whom Marek has never written to (Chapter 0036:89, Chapter 0050:75, and the record above at `He also did not write to Nevin Trost about the ninety words`). Compounding it, the *Write it yourself* beat reversed twice in three lines, and the referents of *it* and *yourself* moved, so a reader could not tell who was asked to write what. **Repaired by splitting the turn and giving every clause to the person it belongs to.** Marek now says the rule is sixteen months old and has been used six times in fourteen months and **has not once in sixteen months been about a person**, which is the figure `outline/volume-04.md:15` gives and which the old text had as *about four months* — a figure that is Tamsin's tenure in the third box, not the rule's age. Tamsin says *a fact is not advice* and *about four months* and *I have never once had it tested like this*, which are hers by three separate chapters. **Marek keeps the Trost material and keeps *I have never written to him*, which is canon and is not changed.** The exchange now runs seven turns with a stable referent: one instruction, one refusal, one offer to write it down in a room instead of a corridor, and Marek naming her third line himself in the last line. **The rule's non-use is still a correct non-use and is still the third anybody has made with it, and `a rule that only ever works in one direction is not a rule, it is a preference` is still said, in Marek's mouth, and the record's rule 24 is still true as written.**
2. **`chapter-0169.md:91` contradicted `chapter-0168.md:3` and the card.** The page said *the district court sits above a shop*; Chapter 0168 and `outline/batches/volume-04-batch-0002.md`'s starting condition both give a low building on a flood terrace with a court room on the ground floor. **One clause repaired to the low building and the ground-floor court room.** The clerk of fifty-five and his nineteen years, the application, the four days and the form are untouched.
3. **`chapter-0169.md:15` contradicted `:29` inside fourteen lines.** *The woman of twenty-four was in the corridor and not in the corridor*, and then she stood at the west end of it for about forty minutes. **Repaired to *was in the building and not in the room*, which is what the scene is and what Ivet Sarn's own reason requires** — a party cannot be a witness, so she is in the building and out of the room. Nothing else in the chapter moved.
4. **`chapter-0163.md:5` had the wrong attendance figure.** *About forty-one people … had held a review*, against *About thirty-one people came* in Chapter 0161, *about thirty-one people in a bay* in the same chapter, and *about thirty-one people were in a room* in Chapter 0170. **Repaired to thirty-one, and the same figure repaired in Marek's line at `:85`**, which had *forty-one people held a review I did not go to* and now says *about thirty-one people sat in a bay*. **About forty-one remains the rotation, about nine of them did not come, and the ninth line of the slate is unchanged** — the two figures are different figures and Chapter 0161 is where that is said.
5. **`chapter-0170.md:117` had `and and`.** **Repaired.** It was the only word-bounded instance in Volume 04; the fifteen hits a plain `grep` returns are *hand and*, *slate in her hand and*, and are not instances.
6. **`workspace/volume-04/batch-0003/PROMPT.md:11` pointed the next phase at a canon-change list that does not exist.** It ordered obedience to *its twenty-two proposed canon changes and its two carried canon changes*. **The Divergences section has sixteen numbered items and its own lead sentence says that none of the following is a canon change, and `state/continuity.md` holds exactly two, both headed *carried and not acted on*. Repaired to say sixteen and two, to say plainly that no longer list exists, and to make this file the authority where the two disagree.** The adjacent *twenty-four rules* claim was checked and is exact — twenty-four numbered items in the Batch 0002 record — and stands.

## The four medium findings, and what each one was

7. **One real breach of the emphasis-per-speech-turn lock**, at `chapter-0163.md:127`, where one uninterrupted turn carried two bold clauses. **The second clause is now plain**, which is how the same paragraph reads at line 123. **Six other candidates the sweep produced are not breaches and were not touched**, because each is separated from the next by narration inside the paragraph and is therefore a different turn: `chapter-0160.md:53`, `chapter-0164.md:37`, `chapter-0164.md:53`, `chapter-0164.md:91`, `chapter-0168.md:81`, `chapter-0169.md:85`. **A later pass must not 'fix' those six.**
8. **The closing inventory had become a fixed shape**, and the batch's own last chapter was the worst case. **Chapter 0170's closing roll-call went from fifteen paragraphs to nine, and from thirty-five lines to twenty-four, which is 16.7% of the chapter's lines against 24% before.** The anaphora is broken twice — *That question has not been answered* and *And a notice on a nail* — so the list is no longer a list of items that all begin the same way. **And the abridgements of the guarantee were undone in all three chapters: Chapters 0161, 0164 and 0170 each dropped a clause the full statement carries — *and inside a guild's blank list, and inside a rotation they have not been asked about* survived in only one of them — and all three now print every clause of it**, including *answerable at any time afterwards by a person answering in its terms*, *there is no such person and there is not going to be one*, and *inside a guild's blank list, and inside a rotation they have not been asked about, and have been told about none of it*. **The guarantee is not paraphrased, not extended and not answered anywhere in the repair, and no child is named.** Chapters 0161 and 0170 now print the statement **word for word identical**, and Chapter 0164 prints every clause of it and differs in one respect only, which is that it says *on that bank* because the chapter has already named the bank. **It is one standing fact and it should read the same way every time it is named.**
9. **Expository narration was still carrying the reveals.** Chapter 0161 ran thirteen non-dialogue paragraphs before anybody spoke, and the batch's own log claimed the residue was gone. **Two blocks are now staged.** Rennick Adley's ninth line is written out as a line he wrote and read back, and Halla Wray says the sentence she will say in a room, instead of the narrator reporting both. The seat, the four shillings a year and the rent of the building are now **Sefa Ild at the west door with a lamp she is not using**, which is where the chapter already had her forty lines later, so her later entrance is strengthened rather than duplicated. **Her arithmetic, the four shillings, the reader's wage and the refusal of the second season are untouched**, and the *arithmetic is not a notice* line is untouched.
10. **`box` was overloaded across at least five referents, and one instrument had two names.** Twenty-four uses in Chapter 0160 and thirteen in Chapter 0167, where most are legitimate — the three ruled boxes on the form, and a cardboard box on a hip. **The one real collision is repaired: the district's flood authority is *the seat* in Chapter 0161 and was *a box* in Chapter 0165, and it is now the seat in both.** The date-collision box in Chapters 0163 and 0165 is a third referent and is a different thing from the ruled box and is left as it is; **a later batch should keep the ruled box, the seat, the cardboard box and the date-collision box as four words and not slide them into one another.**

## Verified clean by the review, and not spent on

The calendar lock, with zero month names and zero weekday names and ten raw grep hits that are all the modal *may*. The forbidden vocabulary, at zero for *exception*, *precedent*, *certification*, *Ashfall*, *Ilyra*, *present holder*, *ninety-second* and *forty-four thousand eight hundred and nineteen*. The building name, *hired stone store* only and never both names in one chapter. No *two hundred and forty yards*. Zero duplicate paragraphs. **And Nevin Trost in Chapter 0170 is not a new figure** — he is at `bible/characters.md:149`, and *a file of his own and a book he keeps at home with the day on it* matches Chapters 0070 and 0074, so the repair did not create a lock-19 violation by keeping him.

## The craft bounds, re-measured on all ten files after the repair

**Both measures, both denominators named.** Emphasis on **lines**, all-lines denominator: **4.3% to 14.8%**, and on **prose text inside `**…**`**, blockquotes out, asterisks out: **11.1% to 18.4%**. **Ten of ten under a fifth on both**, which is the bound in `outline/volume-04.md`. **Per file, lines then text:** 0161 8.7 / 13.3, 0162 11.3 / 16.7, 0163 11.4 / 15.6, 0164 10.8 / 18.8, 0165 7.2 / 17.7, 0166 14.8 / 18.2, 0167 5.5 / 18.0, 0168 12.1 / 11.1, 0169 4.3 / 17.5, 0170 6.9 / 17.2. **Parity test: zero odd blocks in all ten files.** `about nine` runs **2 to 8** across the batch and Chapter 0170 is unchanged at 8. **`fourteen months` is now zero times in Chapters 161–170, and that is deliberate and not an oversight**: the figure attaches to Marek's Stage 2 instrument and the repair did not need it. Zero digits in prose outside headings. The word count of the batch is **28,081** and the manuscript is **616,778**.

## What the repair did not do, and was not going to

**It did not change the plot, and it did not restage anything.** The collision-as-hole reversal, the door-and-wall distinction, Oren Tal's refused first name, Aurelia Pell's margin and her nine minutes, the sheet with a district at the foot of it, the room to be cleared on the fourth, the thirty-one and the nine, the four never asked, the nineteen behind the bank, the Lowcross bill and the guarantee all stand exactly as the batch left them. **It did not open the Ashfall bundle, did not name it, did not answer what Ilyra Kest found, did not reach the midpoint, did not grant a certification, did not pay the Lowcross bill, did not give the thirty-one of Mosswake a seventh column, did not join the two courts, did not open a file of the sixth year and did not begin the romance.** **It proposed no new canon change**, and **the two proposed canon changes above are carried exactly as they were, both still unacted on**, and the fourth open item under the Volume 04 locks — the building's two names — is untouched and still undecided, and the building is still *hired stone store* in the two chapters that name it.

**On the floor.** The floor fixed by the review of Volume 04 Batch 0001 is about 2,600 words a chapter, and a chapter going under it is to be made longer by a scene rather than finished. **The shortest chapter of this batch is 2,777 (Chapter 0175) and the longest is 3,629 (Chapter 0179), and no chapter of the batch is under the floor.** Three chapters were written short on the first pass and **every one of the three was made longer by a scene and not by a paragraph of findings and not by a figure**: Chapter 0174 gained the tallow candle in a tin, the piece of board to stand it on, and the man of twenty who comes down a corridor to be told a day, because a chapter that is nine tenths one long speech in one room is cured by somebody coming into the room or a second object a person can hold; Chapter 0178 gained the roll of holdings and the definition at the back of it, because the record needed a document in a clerk's hands and not another conversation; and Chapter 0179 gained the register, the refusal to correct it, and the counter staying open for two hours underneath the finding, which is what keeps the batch's climax from being a speech. **Nothing in this batch was trimmed to reach a number and nothing was padded.**

## The rules established on the page in this batch, which Volume 04 must then keep

1. **A list of works with no day at the end of it can be ended by a person writing a day on it, and there is no form for it, and there is no form for refusing one either.** A notice is the only kind of sentence in this empire a person can act on the same day, and it gets to be that because a person's name is at the foot of it, and take the name off and it goes on. **The instrument that ends one is a piece of chalk and a hand, and the person who uses it has accepted a duty, and there is no form anywhere for un-accepting one.** And the day has to be in two places: **the chalk on the notice is the half anybody can act on the same day and it can be washed in seconds; the ink in a person's own book with the day on it is the half that is findable and cannot be washed; and there is no form in this empire that asks for both.**
2. **A person who puts a day at the end of a duty is a person who has accepted it.** Said out loud, in a corridor, by the person who did it, and it is the chapter's engine and it is not advice and nobody is thanked for it. **Nobody in this matter has told anybody how long they have, and a clerk of thirty-eight asked for the one thing nobody had ever given anybody, which was a length, and was given about twenty minutes, and a length is a length and not a day.**
3. **A notice is a list of works, and the men on a list of works are working, and a person who is working is not a person in charge of a thing.** Therefore a thing moved on a list of works is, for the length of the road, **in nobody's charge**, and a thing in nobody's charge can be opened by anybody in a lane. **And the reason nobody is going to open it is that it has not happened yet, which is not a reason and is the truth.**
4. **The fourth line of a recorded custody entry cannot be filled by anybody, and that is not an oversight.** The person who takes a thing is a person who is then in charge of it; being in charge of it for about nine days in a district you do not live in is being made a party; **and there is no form in this empire that makes a person agree to be a party.** So a thing can be moved out of a building and be in nobody's charge on a road for about nine days, and the only instrument that would stop it wants a person who cannot be got. **A duty that stops is not a duty that survives stopping, and a person can stop, and a clerk of thirty-eight at a window stopped one by not being in a room she was not asked into.**
5. **A direction that names no person cannot say to whom a thing is produced, and a direction that names a person makes that person served, and served is party, and a party is a person a book can be true about, and there is no form anywhere for taking a party back out of a box.** **So a court direction can be made to change and the price of the change is a person, and in this matter the person it cost was the only person in it who was not a party.** This is the first time in this matter that being right has cost somebody other than the man who asked, and it is the batch's central inversion of the batch behind it.
6. **A court can be made to change a direction and cannot be made to change a copy, and the difference between the two is the whole of what a thing costs.** A copy of a form that is printed in about nine hundred buildings is worth exactly what a form is worth, which is that anybody may have it for nothing. **A copy of ten entries on four sheets can be read and cannot be leaned on, and a grant is findable and there is no way to un-ask, and those two facts are the same fact pointed at two different objects.**
7. **A person in charge of a thing is a person by accident, and the accident is not rare, and it is the same accident in a clerk, a book-keeper and a mason.** There is no form that makes a person be in charge of a thing and there never has been, and the way three of them came by it is that each was the only one left holding the thing — a key on a string, a ledger, a trowel. **And a person in charge of a thing is the only position in this matter that is not a party, which is why a mason can stand in a room and witness what is read and can be asked to open a door, and those are two different things on two different days about two different walls.**
8. **A door in a wall a man is paid to work on is not a seal, it is an obstruction.** A mason opens a sealed door because he cannot get at the wall behind it and the district will not pay him for a wall with mortar in it. **Nobody asked him and he is not going to say he was asked, and the reason he says out loud is that in about four years there is a person who can say a mason opened a door because a man he had met once asked him, and that person would be telling the truth, and it would be the only true thing anybody in that house could ever say about it.** And: **nobody can make him stand in a room and he would refuse to be thanked and he has a boy of nine and is not going to have that boy be a person that somebody comes about.**
9. **A witness is made by being asked and by not being made a party, and those are the two halves of one thing.** A witness is served nothing and is asked everything. **A person who cannot be served cannot be told, and a person who cannot be told cannot be asked whether they are a party, and a person who has never been asked whether they are a party has been made one without anybody doing anything.** A witness can be erased by being made a party, on a form, in a room, in about nine minutes, and no word is struck out of anything, and the form is a document, and a document is findable, and in this case nobody went and found it.
10. **The procedure that makes a witness is five printed lines and it is legible and a reader can follow it, and the fifth has never once been executed in about a hundred and forty years, and it is not secret and it is not hidden and nobody cut it off.** To ask the fifth line's question the person asking has to know what the person in the room is a party to. **The person the fifth line is written for is the second person, and the second person is not a party, and a person who is not a party is not served, and a person who is not served cannot be told.** So the fifth line is a line that cannot be executed by the person it is written for.
11. **The fifth column of a witness register is a copy of the heading at the foot of the sheet, made by hand, in every line, by the second person, out of a habit a hundred and forty years old, and it is not an answer and it is not a gap.** The heading at the foot of the sheet is the office's name and the fifth line sits under it, and **a line under a heading looks like a name**, and a second person copying a sheet copies the heading and the line under it. **So every register in this empire says every witness was told, and the register is the copy, and nobody has compared a register to a form in a hundred and forty years because comparing is work and the work is not anybody's job.** This is Aurelia Pell's method running in the other direction and it is the batch's real finding: **a person can be put into a column by hand and a person can be left out of one by hand, and here nobody took anybody out — somebody simply never put the right thing in, a hundred and forty times, out of habit.**
12. **A form is the only person who can be found, and it is the fifth line and not the register that the finding is in.** A form printed in about nine hundred buildings for about a hundred and forty years is the same document in every copy, and a copy of it is worth what a form is worth, which is that anybody may have it for nothing, **and that is the reason the fifth line was available to the first person who ever read it and was never once done.**
13. **The fifth line can only be asked by a party, and that is the whole of the hundred and forty years.** A party is served and is told things. A second person is not a party and is not told. **So the only person in the room entitled to execute the fifth line is the one person who must not be in the room as a witness, and the fix is a third person, and a third person who is a party pays for it by being served everything said in that room from that hour, and says so out loud before she asks.**
14. **A person being findable is worth more than a machine stopping, and the two are completely different things, and a clerk knows the difference because she makes about nine hundred of the first kind a year and none of the second.** Doing the fifth line once, in pencil, in a kitchen, with a witness who is nineteen and has a bundle of kindling, changed no register and stopped no machine. **What it produced is a person who can stand up in about four years and say that the fifth line exists, that it is printed, that it is a question, and that it was done once, with a date on it and a hand comparable for forty years.** And the register in the next room still says what it has said for a hundred and forty years.
15. **Nobody took anybody out and nobody ever has, and the thing that was done to a family was done by a second person at about the ninth hour copying a sheet and not knowing there was a difference.** It is not a villain and it is not a conspiracy and it is not an office and it is not anybody at all.
16. **A roll of holdings is arranged by street and not by year, and that is the in-world reason no line on it carries a year, and the absence of a date on a line of that roll is not a gap in a record.** The definition of *disputed* at the back of it is a definition of how to write the word down and not a statement about a person — *where a claim is entered and the assent of the claimant is not entered, or is entered and does not carry a day* — **and there is no column in the roll, and none in that definition, and none in any form in the building, that says whether the person whose name it is can be given anything.** A clerk of thirty-four has written the word about four hundred times in eleven years and has never once been asked what she thought it meant and has never once gone and found out.
17. **A disputed claim is a recorded claim, and a recorded claim has a name on it, and a name on a claim is a road, and a road does not care whether the claim can be enforced.** The blanking bought that nothing could be given to him and cost that he is the cheapest person in the empire for anybody who wants a name in a column and nothing behind it. **A person with nothing enforceable behind them can be made to answer for nothing, and the price of a correction made in a clerk's own hand is that her name goes at the foot of about four hundred of them, and a woman with a name at the foot of four hundred corrections is a woman who can be served about all of them.**
18. **The blank-heir test in the original Compact is not a test about being poor.** A candidate for a temporary foundational office must be human, serve at most seven years, be chosen and not inherited, and **hold no enforceable inherited asset or right at the moment of appointment.** A family that holds nothing enforceable is not a poor family, **it is an eligible one**, and the test was written to be passed by a person with nothing, **and nobody tells the person it has been passed, because the person it has been passed for is a person nobody can serve.**
19. **The blank-heir test has been satisfied since the day a name came out of a file, and the person it was satisfied for did not know, and the reason he did not know is the thing that was done to him.** A family that can be given nothing cannot be served; a person who cannot be served cannot be told; a person who cannot be told cannot be asked; **and a person who cannot be asked cannot say no.** She did not conceal it from him. **She made him unservable, and then she could not tell him, and the not-telling was the making, and the making was the not-telling, and the protection is the concealment and the concealment is the protection, and there is no version of it in which those are two things.**
20. **A person made blank is not made safe and the blankness is a door with a person in it and the person is the one who did the blanking, and this is the third time this volume has said it and the first time it has been said about a person who is reading.** It was said out loud by a reader of seventeen on a bank four hundred and thirty miles down this river in the second week of the eighth month of next year and nobody in that bay followed the answer, and this batch follows the answer and it does not improve, **and the answerer is not named in this batch and nobody has been sent to her and nobody is going to be.**
21. **Naming a question is not the same as answering it, and a book in a city has about nine questions in it and not one of them has an answer at the back.** And the reason to keep a question out of a room: **the moment it is in the room it is the biggest thing in the room, and the biggest thing in the room is the thing nobody is looking at.**
22. **A person gets to be private in this empire by nobody being able to say in a room what she is after, and that is the only privacy there is.** It is a mechanism and it is load-bearing and it is worth more than it looks, **and a man who says in a room that he is not going to be the person who takes it off the door is doing something and not saying something.**
23. **Fourpence is not his to withhold.** A person may buy a copy of a record about another person's family and the person the record is about cannot stop it, cannot refuse it and cannot be asked about it, and the clerk who serves it is required to say out loud what a copy is and is not thanked for saying it. **A copy of a thing is a fact about the copying and it will tell a buyer nothing whatever about whether any of it can be enforced, and about four hundred people in a year pay fourpence for a fact about how a book was copied.**
24. **A record is what a person asks for when a person is going to do something with it, and about four years later there is going to be a hearing, and a hearing is a room, and a room is where records are asked for.** Said by a clerk of thirty-four who has been selling copies out of that counter for eleven years and has never once asked a buyer what for.
25. **The rule of the twelfth month of last year does not apply to a person standing in a room on a day.** A rule with a day on it makes a dated thing against a person, and a person in a room does not go in a book with a day on the end of it, because the day on the end of it is how a person gets turned into a duty. **This is the fourth correct non-use anybody has made with it, and the reason is not the reason Chapter 0170 gave, and the count is kept in a copyist's own book.**
26. **A person who refuses to be thanked in advance is almost always believed and almost never taken at her word, and those are the same finding, and it has now been said about two people in this matter and by both of them out loud before anybody started.**

## The calendar of this batch, as printed

**The batch runs from the second week of the eleventh month of next year to the third week of the first month of the year after, which is where `outline/volume-04.md` fixes it and which is Volume 03 Batch 0001's own span of about ten weeks carried forward a year.** Ch 171 the second week of the eleventh month, a notice and a day at the end of it; Ch 172 the **fourth of the eleventh month**, the batch's first deadline and the day the room was going to be cleared; Ch 173 the first week of the twelfth month, a direction granted in a form with a person in it; Ch 174 the second week of the twelfth month, a lane about four miles off the road and a sealed door; Ch 175 the second week into the third week of the twelfth month, inside the house; Ch 176 the third week into the fourth week of the twelfth month, the second person in the room and what she wrote; Ch 177 the first week of the first month of the year after, the fifth line; Ch 178 the second week of the first month of the year after, the third gallery, the fourth counter, a seal and a register read against its form; Ch 179 the second week into the third week of the first month of the year after, the reckoning; Ch 180 the third week of the first month of the year after, the plainest words and the river.

**Seven journeys now, and about forty days of them, out of a wage of seventeen shillings and a penny the week.** Batch 0002 spent five journeys and about thirty days and three pounds and thirteen shillings and threepence. **This batch walks the road twice more and the road down in this batch is walked by a woman of thirty-four who had to say out loud what it costs, which is four days at a counter with nobody at it, and a counter with nobody at it does not open, and there is nobody to cover and no form for covering.** **The road's arithmetic is printed in this batch three times and no new money total is derived anywhere: a day of that wage is a little over two shillings and fivepence, six days is a little over fourteen shillings, and a man of thirty-eight says out loud that he is not going to work out a new total for a woman at a window because a total is a thing a man does once.** A clerk's own day is given as between fourpence and a shilling for a reading and rather more for a day, and the total is not worked out, and a towpath is a short walk and a cart is a day of somebody else's wage.

**Inherited dates spent or named in this batch, none of them moved.** The first season began on the second of the fifth month of next year, is about ninety days, and **its review was spent in Batch 0002 and is not printed here and no figure from it is repeated.** The question bought in the second week of the fifth month of next year at a shilling **is not printed here and no elapsed period is computed from it.** The reader's engagement **is not printed in this batch at all and no elapsed period is computed from it anywhere in the ten files.** The first exception's withdrawal document, dated the twenty-fourth of the ninth month of last year and effective the second of the fifth month of next year, is **not printed.** The first door-to-door asking, the seventh of the seventh month, and the day a chair was fixed, the fifteenth of it, are **not printed.** The Sorn enrolment of the eighth of the seventh month is **not printed.** The refusal of the direction came back in the **fourth week of the tenth month of next year** and is not re-dated, and the reason in it still uses the word *bound* in the middle of the sentence and is quoted whole in Chapter 0173 and not explained. The clearing was named in the **last week of the tenth month of next year** as the fourth of the month after, and **the fourth is spent in Chapter 0172 and is not moved, and the notice gets the day anyway and in two places.** A clerk of thirty-four's own eleven years at the counter and a mason's eleven years patching a wall are durations of their own trades and are not dates in this matter.

**And one date this batch is forbidden to have, and does not have.** **No chapter in Chapters 171–180 prints a date, an age, or a number of years for the arrangement that made the Kest record unusable, for the redaction, for the rows in the register, or for the woman who arranged it, and no chapter says how long ago anything in the Kest file happened.** This is Batch 0001's first proposed canon change, carried and not acted on, and carried again in Batch 0002. **The first draft of Chapters 0176 and 0179 breached it four times with the phrase *about nine years*, describing how long ago the Kest line was written, and once more with *a girl of nine or ten* and *a woman of about nine*, and all six were found and cut before the batch closed and replaced by referring to the thing rather than counting it** — *in all the years I have been at this end of the lane*, *before you wrote a word of that down*, *a small boy*, *years old in her own head*. **The page nowhere says that the woman a man of sixty-one or two was trained by is Ilyra Kest:** she is on the page in this batch as the mother of a man of thirty-eight and as the name in the first column of a register, Oren Tal is not in the batch and is not asked about anything, and the two are not in one sentence as one. **And the page nowhere refers to what Ilyra Kest found as a question:** Marek Kest wants to ask it so badly that he puts his hand flat on a bench twice before he notices he is doing it, and does not ask it, and writes four words in his own hand with the day on them so that the not-asking is findable and a hand can be compared against it for forty years.

## The figures this batch printed, and which of them are new

**Inherited and unmoved, and every one either printed on the page of this batch or carried as a fact:** a shilling for a question at a notary's table; fourpence for a copy; about eleven weeks for an answer; **about four hundred forms in a box under the fourth counter**; a hundred and forty years for the shape of a custody-entry form, a foreman's list of works, a practice, a book of forms, and now a printed witness sheet; forty-five pence a day and four days a week for a reader, and a reader's day between fourpence and a shilling; seventeen shillings and a penny the week; a day of that wage a little over two shillings and fivepence; six days a little over fourteen shillings; **five journeys, thirty days, three pounds and thirteen shillings and threepence out of about forty-four pounds a year, and no fund and no form for a fund**; four hundred and thirty miles each way and about six days and no chapter pretending it is shorter; a hundred and forty yards below the ford; about nine hundred blanks in a box and about nine hundred readings; **the Lowcross bill at nineteen pounds three and fourpence with no line for a bridge in that fund in nineteen years, about a penny a day, four hundred and eleven on the far side and three hundred and eighty-eight crossings**; about four hundred and forty foot of outer face; the thirty-one of Mosswake; about nineteen refusals; about four never asked; about nine hundred and forty names a magistrate made answerable and a guild's hundred and thirty-five shillings. **The box's counts — two hundred and sixty-one empty, a hundred and forty filled, fourteen with a body, eleven with a name and a date in a different hand — are canon, are not printed in this batch and are not altered.**
