## The craft bounds, measured, and the method stated before the claim

The outline binds emphasis at about a fifth of a chapter's **lines** and about a fifth of a chapter's **prose text**, and requires a batch to say which of the two it measured and with what method. **Both were measured, over all ten files, and both hold.**

**On lines:** lines carrying a `**` over all lines, all-lines denominator. **Minimum 4.8% in Chapter 0184, maximum 12.9% in Chapter 0183, median 9.9%.** Ten of ten at or under a fifth. **This is the measure Volume 03 passes on, where the volume runs 2% to 22% with a median of 14%.** Per file, lines: 0181 5.9, 0182 8.0, 0183 12.3, 0184 4.9, 0185 10.6, 0186 7.6, 0187 10.2, 0188 8.6, 0189 11.2, 0190 12.0.

**On prose text:** characters inside `**…**` as a share of non-blockquote characters with the asterisks removed from the denominator, and with the asterisks paired inside the line and never across a blank line. **Minimum 11.1% in Chapter 0182, maximum 18.5% in Chapter 0189, median 15.8%.** Ten of ten at or under a fifth. **This is the measure Volume 03 fails on, where the volume runs 3% to 42% with a median of 23% and thirty-two of fifty chapters are over a fifth, and the batch's median is under a third of the volume's.** A batch that claimed only the lines measure would have been claiming the easy half. Per file, text: 0181 13.6, 0182 11.1, 0183 15.8, 0184 11.7, 0185 18.4, 0186 16.0, 0187 15.9, 0188 16.8, 0189 18.5, 0190 15.7.

**Both measures were re-run after every chapter was edited, because a chapter that is added to has to be re-measured, and nine of the ten were added to or rewritten after a first measurement, and every figure in this section is the figure after the last edit.**

**Chapter 0181 was written in an earlier run of this phase and was preserved by a checkpoint. It was finished prose at 2,656 words and it was not restarted, and it is the one chapter of the batch that was not written in this run.** It was repaired at the line in five places and every one of the five is a finding and none of them is plot. *About four weeks* at a counter became *about three weeks*, because she came back up the road on the sixth day of the first month. *Nine years of standing at counters* became *eleven*, which is the counter's own figure. **Two directions of travel were backwards: the flood terrace is four hundred and thirty miles *down* this river from Auremar and the letter and the closing paragraph both had it up, and the closing paragraph had also given a clerk of thirty-four a key on a string that belongs to a clerk of thirty-eight.** The letter's date moved from the second week to the first week **so that the certification four days later falls in the second week and the notice in Chapter 0182 can stand on ground that already exists**, which is the card's own calendar and the page's arithmetic made to agree. A paragraph that had a clerk looking at a copy in a coat four hundred and thirty miles away was rewritten so that the copy in the coat belongs to the man of thirty-eight who carried it and who said the two sentences about a gap in a copy and a gap in an original, and the clerk was in the room when he said them. The emphasis was trimmed at two speech turns, and about two hundred words were added because the chapter was under its card's band and the cure is a scene, and the scene is a pigeonhole and the difference between a letter a clerk will answer and a letter nobody can be made to produce. **Chapter 0181 is 2,903 words and the batch total in the table at the top of this record, 30,989, is the post-repair measurement and is the one that governs.**

**The pairing test, run because it is the one that produced a false baseline in Volume 03's own review.** A paragraph-level parity test over all ten files, counting every paragraph and never pairing across a blank line, **returns zero odd blocks, and every file has an even number of emphasis marks: 14, 26, 34, 16, 28, 24, 26, 24, 28, 36.**

**No more than one emphasised clause in any one speech turn:** a sweep over all ten files for any paragraph carrying two bold runs with nothing plain between them **returns zero breaches.** **The repair that worked was structural and it is the batch behind this one's repair: every run of more than one sentence was cut back to its first sentence and the sentences that followed were left in the chapter unemphasised.** Nine runs were cut on this pass — Chapter 0181 at two speech turns, Chapter 0183 at six, Chapter 0190 at seven, of which the guarantee and the Lowcross inventory are canon and could not be cut at all and are the reason the batch's prose-text measure is 6 points lower on Chapter 0190 than its first draft was. **The five lines of the printed form and the four definitions of the schedule are quoted in italics inside blockquotes in Chapters 0182, 0183 and 0186 and carry no bold, and the numerals in them were written as words before the batch closed, so that there are no digits anywhere in the batch outside the chapter headings.**

**`about nine`, measured with `grep -o 'about nine' file | wc -l` per file, which is the method the inherited figure was measured with and which counts *about nine hundred*, *about nine minutes* and *about nineteen*.** **Minimum 2 in Chapter 0183, maximum 7 in Chapters 0186, 0187 and 0190, median 5.5, ten of ten at or under the bound of about eight.** The thins were made by deleting a counted clause or referring to a thing instead of its number — *about nine feet of stall and about nine other things on the other boards* became *nine feet* and *nine other things*; *for about nine seconds afterwards* became *on the walk to the cart*; *trying for about nine minutes to find a person to be angry with* became *turning the whole day over since the fifth hour*; *for about nine seconds and then about six of them said it at once* became *for a while*; *about nine hundred buildings with a form in them* became *nine hundred buildings with a form in them*; and *about nine men heard me say it* became *half a yard heard me say it* — **and not by substituting a sibling figure: no figure the state files record verbatim was changed, and `about four`, `about forty`, `about thirty`, `about twenty`, `about sixty` and `about nineteen` were not swapped in for any of them.** Nine hundred is attached to four referents across the batch and all four are the same referent: buildings where a printed form is kept, buildings where a register of witnesses is kept, offices that have the form, and copies a year a clerk sells.

**`fourteen months` is zero times in the batch, deliberately, and the reason is that the page dates the first notice of a seat instead of counting the months to it.** The bound fixed in the review of Batch 0001 attaches the figure to one fact and at most four in a chapter; **this batch had no occasion for it, and the Batch 0004 card's own phrase *fourteen months ago* was not used, and the card's divergence is recorded in the card file item 2.** **No chapter of this batch prints a count of months in running, and no month-count is computed from a dated event: the first notice of a seat is dated on the page and is not counted to, and the fifth line is dated on the page and is not counted to.** The word *months* on the page is attached to a person's own tenure or to a page-months figure a clerk quotes, and to nothing in this matter. **An earlier draft of this record claimed that no chapter printed a number of months anywhere, and the review found *about four months* in five places and *about a month* in two, and the claim here is the corrected one.** A writer who needs a duration in the volume must use the thing's own duration, named from the page, and where the page has none, print none.

**A duplicate audit, run over the ten files, returning one hit and the one hit explained.** Every paragraph longer than eighty characters and every sentence longer than seventy characters was counted across the batch. **Zero duplicate paragraphs. One duplicate sentence, and it is the definition of *of age and resident* out of the schedule, quoted in Chapter 0182 in the room and read out in Chapter 0183 in a corridor to a man who cannot read.** That is the same document read in a second room, and **Chapter 0183 says so on the page before the words are read — *she read the words as they are on the sheet and she did not improve them and she said so before she started, because he was going to have to say them to somebody and the somebody was going to look them up* — so the identical paragraph is an act of the chapter and not an accident of it.** The nine lines in a dead woman's hand are also printed in two chapters, Chapter 0184 whole inside the batch's document and Chapter 0190 by reference, and that duplication is the finding of the batch and is in the card file item 12 and in the record above.

## The two proposed canon changes, carried and not acted on, and one this batch did not propose

1. **The date of the arrangement that made the Kest record unusable is still not reconcilable between the volume outline and the bible, and this batch printed no date for it, no age, and no number of years.** `outline/volume-04.md` and the Batch 0003 phase prompt attach *about thirty-one years ago* to a retired scale notary being trained by a woman called Kest; `bible/characters.md` makes the arrangement an act of Ilyra Kest made twelve years before the opening case. **A man of sixty-one or two with a burn-scarred hand is not in this batch and is not asked about anything and is not referred to at all, and the page nowhere says that the woman he was trained by is Ilyra Kest, and the two are not in one sentence as one anywhere in the ten files.** The winning card is still *print no date, no age, and no number of years for the arrangement, for the redaction, for the rows, or for the woman*, and the page follows it, **and the batch went further than the batch behind it: the published sheet makes the absence of a date a printed, argued and deliberate feature of the document, in four lines, on the page, in his own words.** The disagreement is not resolved by this batch and is not resolved by recording it.
2. **The building is a *hired stone store* on the page six times and a *hired grain store* four times for one building, and neither measurement of the south end of it is on the page.** **Chapter 0188 uses the building and uses one name — *the Slade Cut Company, of the hired stone store off the Slade* — and the south end of it is not measured, and Chapter 0188 does not put the two names in one chapter as though they were two buildings.** This is the third of the three available methods for the fourth open item and the cheapest, because a reader cannot be asked to hold an undecided question about a room the batch names once. **Nobody on the page is told which of the page's two names is right, because it has not been decided.**
3. **A third item, proposed by the page and not by the cards, and it is not a canon change and no decision is asked for.** `outline/volume-04.md` describes what Ilyra Kest did as a *secret exception*, and the same file forbids the word *exception* of anything in Volume 04 that is not a Stage 2 instrument. **The page has the act and not the word, and the act is on the page as a box on a form with nine lines in a woman's hand behind it, and one of those nine lines is now printed in a public document at fourpence a copy in about nine hundred buildings.** If Volume 04's last batch wants the word on the page it will have to bring an instrument with it, and that is a decision for Batch 0005 and not for this one.
4. **A fourth item, and it is new, and it is a finding and not a repair, and no writer needs to decide anything about it.** **The batch established that the notice of a seat names an office as well as omitting a name, in the sixth line, and that this is the first document in this matter to name an office instead of a person.** The state files will carry it as a fact about the document. **It is not a canon change, it does not alter any figure, and Volume 05's question — if the First Custodian was meant to be temporary, who changed it into an inheritable office — is not answered by it and is not touched by it.**

## What this batch owes the fifth batch, in one place

**A notice of a seat with nobody's name on it, and a schedule in a second hand with four definitions in it, one of which turns on a roll of households, and a description with exactly one person in it, and nobody entered and nobody asked.** **A certification with a clerk of thirty-four's hand at the foot of it, in nine seconds, saying the price first, and a printer's man who does not keep a list.** **A wage held in a household of one person, and about forty-one people on a bank held against a company whose whole money is the rent of a roof, and a mason's four days of a shilling, and a clerk of thirty-eight's reading out a definition of *engaged in the matter* in a corridor, and none of it reversed.** **Nine lines published at fourpence a copy, about seventy copies, a heading that says what they are and where they came from, a third column that is not on it, and a printer in a furnace town who set it in type because anybody may have a copy for nothing.** **A woman of sixty-three who came on her own account because a man who cuts kindling read her own hand out loud in a doorway, who has now been given the same answer twice in the same words, and to whom it does not pay either time, and the answer is a hearing and nobody has written the hearing down.** **A reading of ten entries that four people heard and that nobody wrote down, and a clerk of thirty-eight's own book with a day and a tenth term and no name in it, and a mason who has a fortnight's wage held for standing in a room.** **A conversation about protection and secrecy with a day on it, and a thing that has not happened and is not paid, and a woman of twenty-four who has said in advance that she is not going to be told things and has counted her sentences under the table where nobody could see her.** **A refusal to be asked, a new instrument, never used, priced out loud.** **A factor's letter of four lines and nineteen days on a bench, unanswered, and about nineteen people still behind the bank.** **The end of the run, the row, the striking-out, the column headed *by whose authority*, and the name in it, untouched for the fifth movement running. The Ashfall bundle, shut and unnamed, and what Ilyra Kest found, unanswered. And the volume's last chapter: the second season asked for, and about nineteen people who say no again.**

# THE REVIEW AND REPAIR OF VOLUME 04 BATCH 0004, CHAPTERS 181–190

**This section is a self-audit and not the record of a review phase, and it was left here where a later writer would take it for a clean bill of health, and it is not one. It was written at the end of the writer run `next-0002`, out of the writer's own reading of its own ten files. No review step had run against this batch when it was written and none had been asked for, and every one of its fourteen findings is a finding the writer made on its own draft. An independent review ran afterwards and is the last section in this file; it returned thirteen further defects in the ten chapters and three false claims in this section, and every one of the sixteen is answered in it. Where the two disagree, the later one governs.**

**What is true in this section is the line work, and it stands. ## The finding that changed a rule

1. **Chapters 0184, 0185 and 0190 said the second person cannot be found because there is nothing over her; Chapter 0189 said the only reason she is findable is that a second person copied a heading over her, and said both halves in one sentence.** The two accounts ran in opposite directions, and 0189 — the batch's best scene — was arguing against the batch's own evidence. **The reconciliation is that it was never a heading.** The register's fifth column is the office's name in every line and its third column has no heading at all, and that is Batch 0003's canon and it is unchanged. What is in the third column is **a hand**, and a hand is a person in a column exactly as much as a name is, **and a hand is the most findable thing there is: anybody with a copy and about four years can put about four hundred hands side by side and find the one that is hers, and nobody is served anything, no name is said out loud, and there is no form for it and no fee and no day at the end of it.** Chapter 0185 now says that, in a working woman's mouth, as a thing she worked out by counting. Chapter 0189 now says the other half, which is the finding of the conversation and is the reason the sheet is ambivalent: **the act of protection did not take her out of a book. It wrote down the only sentence in the world that says where the books are, put it on a board at fourpence a copy, and told every buyer there are five columns. Not printing the third one is the kindness. Saying there is a third one is the part that is not, and nobody caught him doing it — it is what the doing is.** And the batch's own refusal is now in Chapter 0189, in her mouth: **the register does not travel and the leaf does not travel and the three things a leaf needs are all three required and none of the three has been had, so the finding is not refused and is not given either. It is out of reach, and there is no form anywhere that turns out of reach into a refusal.** This is a rule the volume did not have before and it is the same shape as every other rule in it, and the three places in this run's own record that said *copied the heading* are corrected above and in the other five state files.

- **Chapter 0184 had a doubled section break and a phrase about a passage containing *about nine hundred of nothing else*, which is unintelligible and collided with the locked *about nine hundred buildings* used four other times in the batch for the printed form.** The break is gone and the phrase now says there was nothing else on the boards that had anything to do with anything.

## What the repair did not do, and was not going to

**It did not change the plot.** The notice of a seat still has nothing under the seal and its third line still enters a person with no consent required, and nobody is still entered. The sheet is still published with the third column off it and his name at the foot of it, and the heading that says the register has five columns is still the sentence that ends him. **A wage is still stopped in a household of one person, about forty-one people are still held against a roof, a mason has still lost four days of a shilling and will still not ask for them back, and a factor's letter of four lines is still on a bench and still unanswered.** The guarantee is still standing and unanswered and the Lowcross bill is still unpaid. **Bess Tarrant still came on her own account, still asked whether there is more of her than nine lines, still cannot be told, and still asked the third question and still got the same answer in the same words, because the only change to that answer is that it now says *in a room* where the room is the room she is standing in.** Nobody sent her and nobody is going to.

**It did not open the Ashfall bundle, did not name it, did not answer what Ilyra Kest found, did not join the two courts, did not open a file of the sixth year, did not grant a certification, did not pay the Lowcross bill, did not give the thirty-one of Mosswake a seventh column, did not begin the romance, did not pay the V4 half of the relationship milestone, did not send anybody to the reader and did not name her, did not answer a question on a slate in a counting room in Greyfen, and did not spend the volume's final image.** **It proposed no new canon change, and the two proposed canon changes above are carried exactly as they were and both are still unacted on.** And it created no phase: `workspace/volume-04/batch-0005/` did not exist when the review ran and holds `PROMPT.md` and nothing else.

The section above this one, headed `THE REVIEW AND REPAIR OF VOLUME 04 BATCH 0004, CHAPTERS 181–190`, was written by the writer at the end of its own run and was not the record of any review; it has been corrected where it stands and it is a self-audit. This section is the last section in this file and where the two disagree, this one governs.**

**No chapter was restarted. No date moved. No open thread was closed and none was opened. No canon figure was altered. No chapter of Volumes 01, 02 or 03 was touched and no chapter of Volume 04's first thirty was touched. A wage is still stopped in a household of one person, about forty-one people are still held against a roof, a mason has still lost four days of a shilling and will still not ask for them back, and a factor's letter of four lines is still on a bench and still unanswered.**

9. **`chapter-0181.md` contradicted itself about a woman's tenure.** *The only thing in three weeks of standing at this counter* sat in the same paragraph as *she has been at this counter eleven years*, and the eleven years is canon in six chapters. **It now reads *the only thing since she came down the road*, which is the same fact and is true of both.**

16. **`chapter-0189.md` had a sentence that began with a lowercase *and* after a full stop** and ran to about two hundred words. **The sentence is broken into four and the *and* is a sentence of its own.**

22. **`chapter-0185.md`'s only decision was a refusal to act, and it closed by re-voicing the ending of Chapter 0184.** **She now takes out a second clean sheet and writes a heading over her own count — what a person is owed, by whom, on what day, about the eleven houses and the four other houses and nobody else — and says in her own mouth that a column with a heading over it is a machine for turning one thing into another kind of thing and that she is setting it there on purpose.** Nobody asked her, there is no form for it, no fee, and no column in that town that will take it, and it is hers.

24. **What is left is deliberate and is left.** **Eight chapter pairs share a quoted instrument or a quoted document** — the schedule's four definitions and its wage provision across 0182, 0183, 0186 and 0188; the sheet's first line across 0184, 0185 and 0190; the district form across 0187 and 0188. **One document quoted in four chapters is a document, not a copy-paste, and Chapter 0183 announces the reading on the page before the words are read.** Beyond those, a dozen runs of ten to eleven words are the batch's refrains and its dates: *I am a party to an instrument about a dead woman's name*, said five times in 0182 and the seventh time in 0189 with the count auditable on the page; *there is no form anywhere for taking a party back out of a box*; *there is no form in this empire that makes a person be in charge of a thing*; *a form with a heading over it and no person under it*; the dates. **No shared run between two chapters that is not a quoted instrument or a refrain is longer than eleven words, and there is no duplicate paragraph anywhere in the ten files.**

## The thirty-two rules this batch established on the page, which Volume 05 must then keep

1. **A hearing is a room and a room gets a day, and a date entered in a minute book with a name at the foot of it is a document, and a document is the only instrument this matter has ever had that anybody can be held to.** A notice of a date with nobody's name on it is not a summons to a person.
2. **A date is findable, a notice can be served on nobody, and a date can be stood in by anybody, and the only protection a person has against a day is to be told about it — and being told is a service, and being served is a party, and there is no way back out of a party.** That is the notice's third line running the other way, and it is the sentence Volume 05 inherits whole.
3. **The protection a name at the foot of an entry gives is fourpence of ink and about nine seconds of a woman's time, and it works in one direction: it makes the clerk answerable and it does nothing whatever for the person the date is about.** A clerk of nineteen years said it out loud.
4. **And a clerk of nineteen years who enters what she is given without knowing what it is, and who says in the room that she did not know, is a clerk who was asked — and there is nothing in the world that makes that better or worse, and the only way to find out is to be asked, and the asking is what the machinery cannot do.**
5. **A form printed in about nine hundred buildings can be asked what it means, and nobody has ever asked one, and the fifth line of a printed witness sheet has been dead for about a hundred and forty years because the person it asks is the one person in the room who by definition cannot be told.** A second person cannot be served; being served is what makes a person a party; a party is the only person who can be told what a thing is going to be used for.
6. **The fifth line is the only instrument in this empire that can hand a person the rest of what they wrote, and it is a question, and it has been used once, in pencil, in a kitchen, in about nine minutes, and it is not going to be used again on the same person.**
7. **A form which cannot be asked can still be filled in, and the day it was filled in is a day, and the day is the only part of the whole thing that anybody can find.** Everything else in it is a description and a heading and a thing with no name on it, and a description is not findable.
8. **A person said no in a room, out loud, with the day on it, using the only instrument there is, and the instrument did what an instrument does, which is it exists. A room that writes a no down is not the thing that has the no in it.** That is the sentence a book says four years later about a woman who said no and will not say what the no did.
9. **A company of nine families and about forty-one people on a rotation is a *family* inside the schedule's own definition, and the only person of that company with a place of custom or of work in a roll of households is the foreman whose job was never written down.** So the third line that caught a dyer of twenty caught a foreman of fifty-one eleven weeks later, and the protection that made Halla Wray unfindable for forty-two years is the reason she is findable, and nobody chose it and nobody is going to say the same thing about it twice.
10. **The job that is not written down is the office, and there is no form in this empire that makes a person be in charge of a thing, and a thing nine families agreed to out loud in a shed eleven years ago cannot be produced, and that is the whole of why a foreman is the cheapest person on a bank and the most exposed person on it.**
11. **A hand identified by comparison is a hand nobody can deny, and a delivery stub is the one document in this empire designed to be handed to a person who is not the person it is about.**
12. **A refusal in one form on three days is a person being consistent, and a person being consistent is a document, and there is no form anywhere that requires a person to be consistent, and the fact that a person was is the most exposed thing about him anybody has found this year.** A man could have refused in four different forms and been unfindable.
13. **A file in four places is a file that cannot be lost and is a document that can be produced in four rooms, and the fourth place in this matter is a back room off a corridor a clerk has walked every working day for nine years and has never been inside, and there is no list anywhere in that building that says who is allowed in it.**
14. **The reason nobody has ever been able to find out who did a particular thing to a roll is not that it was well done. It is that it was ordinary, and it will be exactly as true in nine years as it is this evening, and the whole of it is that a person with a pen can put a name into a column and take a name out of a column and there is no instrument anywhere that stops it.**
15. **A person who is a party and is told everything has stopped being at a cost and started being a fact, and a person who is documented is at a different and not a cheaper cost, and the two are not the same instrument and the difference has to be priced out loud because it is about four years.**
16. **A good reason applied unevenly by one person in a district for nineteen years is not a rule and cannot be defended as one, and the second four hundred are the reason the first nine hundred and forty cannot be defended as a rule.** A rule is a thing that is applied the same way each time.
17. **A finding entered against a person by that person on that person's own motion names no person, is appealable by nobody, and is not a discovery and is not a seam, and it binds her and helps nobody, and she made it hers so that it is here.** And a person who names a body in a minute becomes a person whose minute can be asked about, and a minute that can be asked about is a document.
18. **A witness who has been in a room for about an hour and a half and has been given nothing and has been given the only reason anybody ever gave him, and who says he is not owed anything, and who would not have come without the carriage and does not pretend otherwise.**
19. **A procedure is not a person. A record of what a person did in a room is a record of the shape of the room and the order the things were asked in, and the reason the person was in the room is in neither of them, and the reason is the only part anybody has ever wanted.**
20. **The procedure is not a machine for hiding the reason. The procedure is a machine for making sure the reason is not needed, and it does that by not asking, and the not-asking is in the first line.**
21. **The mark on the inside of his left wrist reads nothing, decides nothing, and does not know where the ford is, and there is no office in this empire whose business it is to ask it anything, and the price of what he did in the fourth hour of the second of the fifth month of next year is about forty-four pounds a year and five journeys and thirty days and three pounds and thirteen shillings and threepence gone out of it with no fund and no form for a fund, and the wage is the price and the mark is neither.**
22. **The reconstruction is possible, out of a procedure and out of nothing else, and it will give a shape and not a woman, and that is not a defect in the method, that is the method — and a man who does a thing that cannot give him what he wants is doing a thing that is not heroism and is not cowardice and has no name on any form in this empire.**
23. **A day of a man's own memory is not evidence. It is not in a copy and it is not in a hand anybody can compare, and the one thing a person had that no document in a matter has is the one thing that can be taken out of a book with a pen and a good reason.**
24. **A person who is being comforted has stopped being in the room, and a person who is working has not, and neither of those is coldness.**
25. **A witness status can be restored by a court that finds the record was wrongly kept, and the restoration is a pen, and findable is not a consolation, findable is what a name on a roll is, and there is no way in this empire to put a name back a second time.**
26. **An act done by a person who was not heard cannot be undone by a court that has no power over her and no standing to make one, and the reason is not unwillingness and not lack of power, it is that the person is not alive to be heard, and there is no form anywhere in this empire for a person to be heard after, and the not-hearing is the finding.** And the two are said in one breath, in that order, and the first is not a consolation for the second, and a clerk says before she reads them that anybody who thinks the first makes the second better should leave now, and nobody leaves.
27. **There is no way in this empire to un-undo one either, and a reader is left with two facts and no way of telling which of them the volume is about, and that is not an accident of the finding and it is not a defect in the record. It is what a room is.**
28. **A seat is a thing in a room without being a person. A person who has written nineteen years of minutes about a thing and has never been in the same room with it can tell you nothing about it, and the reason she is the only person in the room who cannot be examined is the reason she is the only person in the room who is paid nothing, and those are the same reason and nobody has ever put them together.** And naming a thing in a room does not put the thing in the room, and a document that names an office is a document and not an office.
29. **Naming a question is not the same as answering it, and the recording of a question is a document, and a document is findable, and a minute book with the day on it and a clerk's name at the foot of it is the only protection a question has ever had in this empire.**
30. **A person who is safe because nobody can instruct her and useful because somebody needs her standing in a room is a person with two boxes filled in on the same form, and a clerk who rules the two boxes by hand and fills in the same name in both of them is telling the truth about a thing that a line under one name would have hidden.**
31. **A thing this empire can put in a book is a thing this empire can ask about, and there is one thing in a room that is not going in a book, and it is not going in a book because neither person is going to write it down, and a person remembering a thing and a person reading a thing back are two different acts and only one of them is evidence.**
32. **The third thing has no box, and there is no form in this empire that will hold a sentence a man has not finished, and a person cannot be a party to a thing that is not finished, and that is the first good thing anybody has said in this matter since the first week of the fifth month, and it was written on nothing.** And: **a fact said in a room with two people in it is the only kind of fact in this empire that is not evidence of anything, and two people would rather have that.**

## The locks, checked over the ten files, and how

Every one of these was searched over `chapters/volume-04/chapter-019[1-9].md` and `chapter-0200.md` and held, and the method is given because a claim of absence is cheap and a claim of uniqueness is the one that costs.

- **Calendar month names and weekday names.** `grep -rniE "\b(january|february|march|april|may|june|july|august|september|october|november|december|monday|tuesday|wednesday|thursday|friday|saturday|sunday)\b"` over the ten files returns **eighteen lines and every one of the eighteen is the modal verb *may* or the phrase *may as well*, in six files, and no month name and no weekday name appears anywhere in the batch.** **Two were written during this run and both were found by the check and cut before the batch closed**: *Thursday*, in the last line of the fair copy in Chapter 0196, rewritten to *the fourth day of next week*; and *April* and *March*, in Rennick Adley's speech in Chapter 0200, where he names the two months two men in this matter did a thing, rewritten to the second day of the second week of the fourth month and the third week into the fourth week of the third month. **Zero digits in prose outside the chapter headings.**
- **The forbidden vocabulary.** **The word *exception*: zero. The word *precedent*: zero, including of the river matter Leda Rell testifies about, which the page calls a river and a decision and a reasoning in a minute and never a name. *Ashfall*: zero. *the present holder*: zero. *ninety-second*: zero. *forty-four thousand eight hundred and nineteen*: zero.** *exception* is zero of anything, including the act `outline/volume-04.md` calls Ilyra Kest's secret exception, and **the act is on the page as a box on a form and nine lines in a woman's hand, and Chapter 0197's finding describes it in four sentences without a word for it, and the word is nowhere.** *Venn* and *ruling* are zero and this batch refers to the schedule on the rail **zero times**, as the batch behind it did. *the counting-house mark*, *the year in the run*, *the sixty-fourth leaf*: zero and not mentioned. **The quarterly return does not appear on the page in this batch at all and is still in no reply. Hallis Dren's return of the eleventh of the tenth is dormant, armed, and known to nobody in the story, and neither document is named in Chapters 191–200. The four appearances of the substituted wording keep their four ages and are not in these ten files and no fifth was added.**
- **The three Orises and the name at the foot of a notice.** *Seryn Oris*, *Sivra Oris* and *Vaunt Oris* are **zero across the ten files.** The holder of the office of the seat is not named and is not present and is not examinable and is credited with nothing, and **Chapter 0197 enters on the record that a question about whether a seat gave an order in this matter cannot be answered, that the only document that would bear on it is a document that cannot be produced by anybody, and that the document is a notice in six numbered lines with a seal at the foot and under the seal there was a name once — and that the clerk declines to say the name or the hand or which of the two notices it is, and asks for it to be entered that she declined and was asked and was not pressed.** The name is not said aloud in that room or in any other.
- **The three red things, the two sealed pages, and the sealed witness house.** The three red things are not named in any of the ten files. ## The craft bounds, measured, and the method stated before the claim

The outline binds emphasis at about a fifth of a chapter's **lines** and about a fifth of a chapter's **prose text**, and requires a batch to say which of the two it measured and with what method. **Both were measured, over all ten files, and both hold. The measures are named before the claim, as this batch requires.**

**On lines:** lines carrying a `**` over all lines, all-lines denominator, chapter heading excluded. **Minimum 8.9% in Chapter 0191, maximum 14.2% in Chapter 0197, median 10.9%. Ten of ten at or under a fifth.** This is the measure Volume 03 passes on, where the volume runs 2% to 22% with a median of 14%, and the batch's median is three points under the volume's. Per file, lines: 191 8.9, 192 9.5, 193 13.9, 194 9.6, 195 10.1, 196 10.1, 197 14.2, 198 13.1, 199 11.8, 200 11.5.

**On prose text:** characters inside `**…**` as a share of non-blockquote, non-heading characters with the asterisks removed from the denominator, and with the asterisks paired inside the paragraph. **Minimum 12.3% in Chapter 0192, maximum 19.1% in Chapter 0197, median 15.6%. Ten of ten at or under a fifth.** This is the measure Volume 03 fails on, where the volume runs 3% to 42% with a median of 23% and thirty-two of fifty chapters are over a fifth, and the batch's median is a third under the volume's. **A batch that claimed only the lines measure would have been claiming the easy half.** Per file, text: 191 16.5, 192 12.3, 193 17.4, 194 14.6, 195 15.8, 196 14.0, 197 19.1, 198 16.6, 199 18.8, 200 15.3.

**Both measures were re-run after every chapter was edited, because a chapter that is added to has to be re-measured, and every figure in this section is the figure after the last edit.** Seven of the ten were over a fifth on the text measure in a first measurement and **the repair that worked was structural and not lexical: a run of more than one sentence was cut back to its first sentence and the sentences that followed were left in the chapter unemphasised, and a long single-sentence run was split so that its first clause carried the emphasis and the rest did not, and not one word of prose was changed to do it.** Chapter 0192 was at 26.5% on the text measure in its first measurement and Chapter 0197 at 32.8% and Chapter 0199 at 37.3% and Chapter 0200 at 22.1%, and all four are the chapters that carry a document or a speech, and the two that carry the most document — 0197's finding and 0200's guarantee — are the two highest figures in the batch, **and the guarantee is canon word for word and could not be cut at all, which is the same cost Batch 0004 recorded and reported rather than broke.**

**The pairing test, run because it is the one that produced a false baseline in Volume 03's own review.** A paragraph-level parity test over all ten files, counting every paragraph and never pairing across a blank line, **returns zero odd blocks, and every file has an even number of emphasis marks: 28, 26, 26, 26, 26, 24, 36, 28, 36, 28.** One unclosed bold run was written during this run, in Chapter 0191, in a speech turn, and was found by the parity test and closed.

**No more than one emphasised clause in any one speech turn:** a sweep over all ten files for any paragraph carrying two bold runs with nothing plain between them **returns zero breaches.**

**`about nine`, measured with `grep -o 'about nine' file | wc -l` per file, which is the method the inherited figure was measured with and which counts *about nine hundred*, *about nine minutes* and *about nineteen*.** **Per file: 6, 8, 3, 5, 6, 8, 6, 3, 5, 6. Maximum 8, against a bound of about 8 a chapter, ten of ten at or under it, and the thins were made in Chapters 0192, 0193, 0194 and 0196 by deleting a counted clause or referring to a thing instead of its number** — *about nine hundred buildings in this empire, and a stack of them is on a table in this room about nine inches deep* for *it is in about nine hundred buildings in this empire and it is in about nine hundred of them in this room in a stack on a table and about nine hundred of them have never been looked at* — **and not by substituting a sibling figure: no figure the state files record verbatim was changed, and `about four`, `about forty`, `about thirty`, `about twenty`, `about sixty` and `about nineteen` were not swapped in for any of them.**

**Month-counts.** **`fourteen months` is zero times in the batch, deliberately, and the page dates everything instead of counting to it.** **No chapter of this batch prints a duration counted in months anywhere.** Every instance of the word in the ten files is either a calendar month, and there are ninety-one of them, or the one inherited phrase about a second season being in its fourth month, which is a calendar reference and not a count. **Twenty-five instances of *about four months* and *about two months* were written during this run and every one of them was found by the closing check and cut before the batch closed, and the cure in each case was to date it** — *in the second week of the first month*, *since the third month*, *in the fourth week of the fourth month*, *between the first and the fourth month of this year*, *since the second week of the seventh month* — **and not one was replaced by a sibling duration.** The measure is claimed as: no duration counted in months is printed, and no month-count is computed from a dated event, and the first notice of a seat is not in this batch and the fifth line is not in this batch and neither is counted to.

**A duplicate audit, run over the ten files.** Every paragraph longer than eighty characters and every sentence-like segment longer than twenty-five characters was counted across the batch. **Zero duplicate paragraphs. Ten shared segments between two chapters, and every one of them is accounted for.** Five are the five printed lines of the sheet a witness is entered upon, quoted in Chapter 0192 in a hearing room and quoted in Chapter 0196 in a hired room, **and Chapter 0196 announces the second reading on the page before the words appear, the way Chapter 0183 announced its reading before it read, so the identical quotation is an act of the chapter and not an accident of it.** Two are the sentences that identify a point of view — *Marek Kest is thirty-eight* and *Tamsin Rook is twenty-four* — which are the house convention and appear in every batch of the volume. Two are the batch's own refrains: *it went in with the day on it* in Chapters 0197 and 0200, and *it is not going to be answered* in Chapters 0198 and 0200, both about the factor's letter and both the same fact. One is the double reading's reason in Chapters 0198 and 0200, a bank-keeper's sentence about a column for four people who cannot read a paragraph. **No shared run between two chapters that is not a quoted instrument, a point-of-view identification, or a refrain is longer than eleven words.**

## The proposed canon changes, carried and not acted on, and the two this batch did not propose

1. **The date of the arrangement that made the Kest record unusable is still not reconcilable between the volume outline and the bible, and this batch printed no date, no age, and no number of years for it.** `outline/volume-04.md` and the Batch 0003 phase prompt attach *about thirty-one years ago* to a retired scale notary being trained by a woman called Kest; `bible/characters.md` makes the arrangement an act of Ilyra Kest made twelve years before the opening case. **A man of sixty-one or two with a burn-scarred hand is not in this batch and is not asked about anything and is not referred to at all, and the page nowhere says that the woman he was trained by is Ilyra Kest.** The winning card is still *print no date, no age, and no number of years*, and the page follows it, and this batch goes one step further: **Chapter 0197's finding describes the act itself in four sentences — a box on a form printed in nine hundred buildings, filled in by a person with authority to fill boxes, in a room, with a second person in it who was not a party and could not ask anything, and nine lines in a woman's hand — and does not need a date and does not say what it was for.** The disagreement is not resolved by this batch and is not resolved by recording it.
2. **The building is a *hired stone store* on the page four times in Chapter 0200 and a *hired grain store* nowhere in the batch, and neither measurement of the south end of it is on the page.** This is the third of the three available methods for the fourth open item and the cheapest, because a reader cannot be asked to hold an undecided question about a room the batch names once. **Nobody on the page is told which of the page's two names is right, because it has not been decided, and this batch did not decide it and says so.**
3. **A third item, carried and not acted on, unchanged in the fourth batch running.** `outline/volume-04.md` describes what Ilyra Kest did as a *secret exception*, and the same file forbids the word *exception* of anything in Volume 04 that is not a Stage 2 instrument. **The page has the act and not the word, and after this batch the act is described in a public finding without a word for it, and the act cannot be undone and the word is not available.** If a later volume wants the word on the page it will have to bring an instrument with it, and there is none in this batch.
4. **A fourth item, carried, unchanged: the notice of a seat names an office as well as omitting a name, in its sixth line, and that is the first document in this matter to name an office instead of a person.** After this batch it is also the reason a question about whether a seat gave an order **cannot be answered in about four years by anybody**, and the reason is not caution, it is that the only document that would bear on it is a document that cannot be produced. **A document that cannot be produced is a stronger wall than a document nobody has read, and that is a change in the shape of the problem and not in its size, and Volume 05 inherits it.**
5. **A fifth item, new to this batch, and it is a finding and not a repair, and no writer needs to decide anything about it.** **A form printed in about nine hundred buildings was asked what a word on it means, for the first time in this empire, on the fourth day of the second week of the fifth month of the year after, by a room, and the clerk answered and the answer went into a minute and she priced the answer out loud first.** This is the first time in one hundred and forty chapters that the machinery has been pointed the other way, and it was not done by an advocate and it was not done by a party: it was done by a room that wanted a record, for the ordinary reason that a room wants a record. **It is not a precedent and it is not a rule and no form anywhere requires it, and therefore it will not happen again by itself, and the whole of the finding is that a thing which has never happened can be made to happen by a person asking a question, and there is no post in this empire whose job is to do that.**

## THE CLOSE OF VOLUME 04, and what it hands to Volume 05

**Volume 04, *The Missing Copyist*, is closed at Chapter 200 in 148,482 words across fifty chapters, and it is the last movement of a volume that ran in five movements of about ten weeks with the gaps between them and did not close them.**

**What Volume 04 resolved, item by item, against `outline/volume-04.md`'s *Concrete resolution*.**

- **Marek's Kest claim is still undecided and is still open at a counter to anybody, and the redaction stands because he agreed to it in a room with a clerk as his only witness.** **Resolved, in that the volume ends with the claim still undecided and says so, and in that nobody entered anybody and nothing was paid.** The notice of a seat is still in a press in four bays with a seal and nothing under the seal, and its schedule is still unsigned and undated beside it, and neither can be produced in a room by anybody.
- **Ilyra is no longer legally erased: her name is restored to a roll and her witness status is restored, and the restoration is entered with a day on it and a name at the foot of it, and it is findable, and there is no way in this empire to put a name back a second time.** **Resolved, and paid in full in Chapter 0197 and Chapter 0200.** The name went onto a roll in a press in a building in a city, in a clerk's own hand, with the day against it, and the clerk asked for a different pen because the first had been in a pocket, and the second box on the volume's final form at the fourth counter has that name in it.
- **The Cinder Clause is named as a historical question and is not explained: a court records that the question exists, that it has never been answered in nine years by the court that asked it, and that naming it is not the same as answering it.** **Resolved, and it is the only word of the clause in one hundred and fifty chapters of prose and there is one occurrence of it in the manuscript, in a clerk's mouth, in a room with a rail in it, in the last sitting.** It is entered in a minute book with the day on it and her name at the foot of it, **which is the only protection a question has ever had in this empire, and it has cost about nine seconds.**
- **Magistrate Rell testifies about the river precedent and begins to shift from institutional opponent to accountable witness, and the shift is not absolution and it is not a conversion and is entered as testimony in a room with a witness in it.** **Resolved, and the word *precedent* is not on the page anywhere in Volume 04, and the page calls it a river and a decision and a reasoning in a minute.** She has given up the marble thing about a rule, has said out loud that a good reason applied unevenly by one person for nineteen years is not a rule, has still named no person, has given the reason in the first person and had it entered, and has said that a finding entered against oneself on one's own motion names no person and is appealable by nobody and is not a discovery and is not a seam. **A witness was in the room: a man of about seventy-four who had somewhere to go, who gave his name into a record and was asked what he wants and said he is not owed anything.** She was not thanked and did not ask and there is no form that requires it.
- **And the river is still running: the second season of about forty-one people is asked for and about nineteen will say no again, and the guarantee is still standing offered and unanswered with about sixty children inside it, and the Lowcross bill is still unpaid and nobody is still liable, and the thirty-one of Mosswake are still thirty-one, and the volume closes its own immediate promise and opens the next one and does not pretend the river is finished.** **Resolved, in full, in Chapter 0200, and it is the last chapter of the volume.** The second season was asked for in a bay by a man who said out loud that he had been asked to ask and had not volunteered; a carter was first on the list of works and said no again in the same words with the same reason; about nineteen people said no again, one after another, and every one of the nineteen reasons was entered in the place where the no is, and the shortest of the nineteen was four words long. **The guarantee is printed whole and word for word. The Lowcross bill is at nineteen pounds three and fourpence and nobody is liable. The thirty-one of Mosswake are thirty-one, once, in one sentence.** The hold is still in force. The factor's letter is still on a bench. About four people who cannot read a paragraph were never asked once and were not asked on the day.
- **The power change: Marek reaches Echo-Walker only after a failed reconstruction costs him a day of memory, and the cost is named as a loss of what he can remember and not as a number, and it changes who trusts his judgment, because Tamsin is the person who has to decide whether to trust it.** **Resolved as to the attempt and the cost, and deliberately not resolved as to the trust.** He attempted it, it failed, and it cost him **the sixth day of the third month, when he was eleven, and he can no longer remember whether he left the room or stood in the doorway.** **The decision about whether to trust his judgment is not made in a room, is not on the page, and is not going to be made in the next four chapters, and that is the debt the volume hands over and the first thing Volume 05 has to decide what to do with.**
- **The relationship change: the romance begins after a clear conversation about the difference between protection and secrecy, in a scene of its own with a day on it, late, and not a reward for the hearing and not a reward for the power and not a reward for the memory.** **All of that resolved, and the scene of the conversation is Chapter 0189 and the scene of the thing itself is Chapter 0199, three weeks later, on a day on which nothing has happened, and Chapter 0199 says so in its first paragraph.** The two boxes on one form are both filled and the page is honest that a person who is safe because nobody can instruct her and useful because somebody needs her is a person with two boxes filled in on the same form; the paper and the watch are two instruments and the volume says which is which and does not merge them; the rule of the twelfth month of last year is not used and the correct non-use is entered as a use; the first thing either of them did that no form in this empire requires was done, and **it is not entered, and about four hundred and thirty miles of road is what it costs anybody who wants to see it, and there is no fund.**

**What Volume 04 did not resolve, and hands on whole.** The act done by a person who was not heard is not undone and cannot be, and there is no way in this empire to un-undo one either. Nobody can say whether a seat gave an order and the document that would prove it cannot be produced. A woman of sixty-three is not on any roll and cannot be put on one, and a date four years off is in a minute book for a room she is not in and has not been told about. **Two people have now been entered as representatives and neither was asked, and one of them is a foreman of fifty-one whose job was never written down.** A wage is held in a household of one person and about forty-one wages are held against a roof and a mason's four days of a shilling a day are held and a book-keeper's factor's letter is on a bench and the man who put the roof in the box has not been thanked. The reader of seventeen has been in the same bay twice and has not been spoken to about anything. About nine hundred and forty people are made answerable and about four hundred were not, by one person, by hand, on purpose, with a reason that reads like sense, and she has named nobody. A foreman of fifty-one is owed a second sentence and is not going to be asked for it. The end of the run, the row, the striking-out, the impression, the column headed *by whose authority* and the name in it are untouched, now for the sixth movement running. The Ashfall bundle is shut and unnamed and what Ilyra Kest found is unanswered. The two sealed pages are shut with two refusals between them and no third. The two documents are two documents about four hundred and thirty miles apart and only two people know both exist. The quarterly return is in no reply. Hallis Dren's return of the eleventh of the tenth is dormant, armed, and known to nobody in the story. **The clause is named and is not explained and the second half of the volume's question — why dragons themselves are bound by the altered compact — is not asked and is not going to be asked by the next volume either.**

**What Volume 05 opens on.** Two people entered and neither asked, and one of them is on a bank four hundred and thirty miles down a river and is holding a sheet with a seat's device on it that she read twice. A date four years off in a minute book for a question nobody can be asked. A clause named once. A seat that is a thing in a room without being a person and an order that cannot be proved or disproved. A day of a man's own memory gone, and a woman in four bays who has not decided whether to trust his judgment. A third thing with no box, and a form printed in about nine hundred buildings that was asked what it means for the first time in this empire and will not be asked again by itself because there is no post whose job it is. A bundle on a fourth shelf marked *damaged, four items, uncollated*, twelve years old, not opened, not named, a location and not a discovery. A door that is open with nothing come through it yet. About two hundred and forty people who have never known the fourth space is there. A carter of thirty-one who asked to be asked last and was written first, and who said no again. **A reader of seventeen on a written engagement at forty-five pence a day, and this is the last season in which anybody on that bank can ask her something and be answered for nothing.**

**The first figure and the first date of the next volume's calendar.** **The first figure of Volume 05 is a hundred and forty: the years a printed witness sheet, a practice, a bound register, a form, a book of forms, a second person's copying habit, a third column with no heading over it, a procedure and a question have been on the page without a word for it.** **The first date is the first week of the ninth month of the year after**, which is the Batch 0001 span of `outline/volume-05.md` and the month after the last week of the seventh month in which Volume 04 closed. **The first week of the ninth month is the week after the adjournment, the hearing, the restoration, the day that is gone, the hearing in a shed, the room with the door open, and the bay in which about nineteen people said no again, and nothing in it is closed and the first thing in it is a season that nobody has agreed to and a woman who has been entered and cannot get out.**

**And the two lines of `outline/series.md` that are false, restated here because this is the section a Volume 05 writer will read.** **The first is the plan's central pressure for Volume 04, which says Marek's investigation threatens *his certification*. He has none. His bar was discharged on the twelfth of the ninth month of last year by a one-line application he wrote himself, no certification has been granted in any of the four closed volumes, and Chapter 0196 says in his own mouth that he has no certification and no register and no office and a discharged bar and a line about two inches long on the inside of his left wrist that reads nothing, and that the only instrument he has ever been given for the thing he attempted is that line.** **The second is the plan's climax for Volume 05, which says *Marek publicly withdraws his certification for one year and accepts joint liability for the flawed exception*. Both halves are unavailable to him: he has held no certification at any point in four closed volumes and holds none now, and he cannot accept joint liability for an act that was not his and could not have been his, because a person who was not heard is not a person who can be sued and the act is one she made in a room in pencil and a box went to a roll.** Neither is paid in Volume 04 and neither may be paid in Volume 05. **What goes in that place is not decided here and `outline/volume-05.md` does not decide it, and a writer who reads only `outline/series.md` in the ninth month of a year will inherit the false premise unless the new file says it, and the new file says it.**

## The rules established on the page in this batch, which Volume 05 must then keep

1. **A form which cannot be asked cannot be un-filled, and it cannot be un-filled by the person who filled it.** Said in Orla Denning's mouth, Chapter 0201, first week of the ninth month, with a tray on it and a file head with two lines on it. It is in none of the eleven books and she has looked.
2. **The only thing standing between a person in a box and the rest of their life is somebody asking a question out loud in a room, and there is no post in this empire whose job is to ask.** Said in Marn Ottery's mouth, Chapter 0202, second week of the ninth month, standing up at a counter.
3. **A person who has not been served cannot refuse to be served, and a class is not served on anybody, so the only instrument this empire has for saying no is no use at all to a person entered by a class.** Said in Halla Wray's mouth, Chapter 0204, fourth week of the ninth month, to about nine men in a shed.
4. **The three above are the whole spine and no chapter states them together and no state file's compressed form is quoted on the page.** The page's own wording of a compressed version of this spine remains the keeper of a district water office in Chapter 0102, in three parts, and this batch does not quote it either.
5. **A tray does not get asked a question. A woman standing at a counter does, and the woman answers, and there is not going to be a post for it.** Chapter 0201. This is what keeps the count of askings at three, and it is the batch's own answer to its own question.
6. **The only thing standing between a person in a box and the rest of their life is a person, and the price of being that person is that they become answerable for the answer.** Said in Ivet Sarn's mouth before she answers, Chapter 0205, and in Tamsin Rook's mouth, Chapter 0207, and paid in Orla Denning's mouth in Chapter 0209, where the answerable person is the clerk and not the asker.
7. **A record of a document is not a record of a person.** Halla Wray, Chapter 0204, and the reason she entered six numbered lines and a seal and nothing under the seal and refused to enter herself anywhere.
8. **A person who is paid to read is a person who can be told to stop, and that is the whole of the reason, and it is the reason the four are not asked.** Rennick Adley, Chapter 0206, and Halla Wray credits it in Chapter 210 without claiming it.
9. **A refusal is a thing a person is entitled to make once and have it kept and not be troubled about it again, and there is no form anywhere in this empire that entitles anybody to be troubled twice.** Halla Wray, Chapter 0210, first week of the eleventh month.
10. **Being unfindable is the reason a person was never asked and is not the reason she was safe.** Bess Tarrant, Chapter 0208, in her own mouth, and it is the turn of the batch.
11. **A person who comes on her own account is a person there is no form for, and that is the only instrument she has ever had.** Chapter 0208, said twice, by two people, about two people.
12. **The office of a seat keeps minute books and not entries, and an entry goes onto a roll in a district, and there is no instrument that joins the two ends, and the number of the class therefore cannot be told by anybody who would be the person to tell it.** Chapters 0203 and 0209, in Marek Kest's mouth and in Orla Denning's, and the two are the same finding from two ends.
13. **A return carries the office's day and not the keeper's day, and there are two days and one of them is on the paper.** Chapter 0205.
14. **What goes in the box is whatever the roll of households has, and a roll of households has a household in it, and there is no box in this empire for the difference between a person and a trade.** Chapters 0203, 0205 and 0209, said three times by three people and never improved.
15. **A memory of two is worse than a figure of none, because a figure of none is a thing a man can look for and never find, and a memory of two is a clerk of fifty-five in a room with a pane out of the window.** Orla Denning, Chapter 0209, and it is why the batch has two known members of a class nobody can count.

## The craft bounds, measured, and the method stated before the claim

**One. Emphasis, both measures, method first.** **The governing measure is the text measure**: prose characters inside paired `**` runs over prose characters, where prose is every non-blank line that is not a chapter heading, and where runs are paired per file after a per-paragraph parity check. The parity check is clean: **every one of the ten files carries an even number of emphasis marks, and no paragraph in any of the ten files carries an odd number.** On the governing measure the batch runs **9.2% to 18.7%, median 14.5%, ten of ten under a fifth.** **The all-lines measure is reported and does not govern**: non-blank prose lines carrying at least one mark over non-blank prose lines, on which the batch runs **8.9% to 18.5%, median 12.6%**, ten of ten under a fifth and ten of ten inside the inherited Volume 03 all-lines band of two to twenty-two per cent. The first draft of Chapter 0202 was at **24.6% on both measures** and was brought down to 12.8% and 18.5% **by splitting four long single-sentence runs so that the first clause carries the emphasis and the rest does not, and by cutting two runs of more than one sentence back to their first sentence, and by removing one run entirely. Nothing was cut to reach a number and no canon document was touched.** **Seven runs of more than two sentences were found across the batch and all seven were cut back to their first sentence**, in Chapters 0203, 0204, 0205, 0207, 0208, 0209 and 0210. **The per-speech-turn sweep is clean at zero breaches: no contiguous run of one speaker's dialogue carries more than one emphasised clause.** Eight did, and each was fixed by removing the later run and leaving its words in the chapter unemphasised. **A blockquoted form, a minute entry, a schedule and a finding keep their own typography, and that is the document and not a default** — the one blockquoted finding in Chapter 0206 carries no emphasis at all. **`**` is paired inside a paragraph and never across a blank line, and no run opens before an opening quotation mark.**

**Two. `about nine` is bound to about eight per chapter and is thinned only by referring to a thing instead of its number.** The batch runs **3 to 7, median 6, fifty-nine instances across ten chapters, ten of ten under the bound.** No instance was changed to a sibling figure and no sentence was thinned by substituting one. The variation lock holds: `about four`, `about forty`, `about thirty`, `about nineteen`, `about twenty`, `about sixty` are the sibling figures in this batch and none was substituted for another.

**Three. `fourteen months` is used zero times, deliberately, and no number of months is printed anywhere in the batch.** See the calendar checks above.

**Four. The state files are archives and they do not all run the same way.** `state/current.md` is **newest-first** and carries a read cap at its own head: this run read the header, the ownership list and the standing lists and did not read the superseded batch records underneath them, and did not delete them. `state/continuity.md`, `state/batch-summary.md`, `state/open-threads.md`, `state/chapter-summaries.md` and `state/character-state.md` are **append-only downward**, so this record is at the bottom. `grep -n` was used to find every heading and only the range under it was read. **No state file was read whole and no section restates what is already recorded above it.**

**Recorded here because a writer who opens these files needs to know they were not written in one pass.** **Thirty-one sites at which a capital letter or a short capitalised word had been deleted at the start of a clause**, leaving a lowercase word after a full stop or a double space after punctuation; **nine places where the same damage had carried an emphasis marker out of position**, so that a run opened at the start of a speech turn and closed mid-clause several lines later, or was left with a third unpaired marker in its paragraph; **two missing closing quotation marks**, one at the end of a speech turn in Chapter 0203 and one at the end of a speech turn in Chapter 0202; and **one paragraph of stray indentation** in Chapter 0203. **All thirty-one letters are restored, all nine marker positions are repaired, both quotation marks are restored and the indentation is cut.** The tests that found them are: a search for punctuation followed by two spaces, a search for a period followed by a lowercase word, a search for an emphasis marker adjacent to a lowercase letter or inside a word, a per-paragraph parity test on `**`, and a test for a last-of-turn dialogue paragraph whose quote count is not two. **All five are re-run clean over the ten files.**

## The proposed canon changes, carried and not acted on, and the one this batch did not propose

**Carried, unchanged, and not fixed by this batch:** the four open items above; the six copies never made and the eighteen returns that did not come back, which nobody adds together; the fifth line of a witness form, dead for about a hundred and forty years; the third box on the notary's sheet, filled with a description and not a name; the bundle marked *damaged, four items, uncollated* on a fourth shelf, not opened and not named; the date four years off in a minute book; the Cinder Clause, named in Chapter 0197 and unanswered in nine years; and the four names at the foot of the Venn ruling's operative terms, of which the fifth term's schedule went on the rail on a date printed nowhere.

**Not proposed by this batch.** Two things a writer might expect a movement to do and this one did not do, and both are recorded so that nobody goes looking for them. **The batch proposes no new canon figure and no new date for anything inherited.** And it does not decide the thing the volume outline left open: **whether what replaces the false climax is a liability Marek Kest cannot refuse or a labour he can be refused. The batch builds neither and earns neither, and what it does put on the page is the shape both of them need — a person with nothing enforceable behind him, no office, no fund, a discharged bar, and a line about two inches long on his wrist that reads nothing, which Chapter 0207 says in Tamsin Rook's mouth is the reason he is the most dangerous person in this matter and also the reason nobody in it can protect him.** That decision is still a decision for the movements that come after this one and it is not taken here.

## What this batch owes Batch 0002, in one place

1. **The ten open questions in the batch card's closing section, carried unchanged.** The first of them is the one the volume turns on: **who asks**, given that three rooms have now asked a form a question, two of them by accident, one on purpose, and that no post in this empire has it as its business.
2. **A chapter that ends on a decision and not on a cliff.** Chapter 0210 ends on a foreman's decision, in her own words, with the reason given out loud and then named as a bad one. Batch 0002 needs at least one more, and it needs a different person's.
3. **A woman of sixty-three who has decided to go and stand in a room where boxes are filled in and has not gone there yet.** She is at the last week of the eleventh month and the room is in Auremar, and nobody sent her, and the date four years off is in a minute book in that building and is about her.
4. **A woman of twenty who has four people to ask and has asked one of them and has not asked the other three, and a clerk of thirty-four who has refused to write a sentence of her own into a book with no office on it and has said in a room that she is not going to be able to do it.**
5. **A man of about thirty-four at a window who said he would rather not have asked, and who is now answerable for the answer, and who does not know what the answer was.** Nobody has told him. That is the cost the batch planted and did not spend.
6. **The river, and the four who cannot read a paragraph, and a reader of seventeen who is the wrong person to ask and the only one free to answer, and this is the last season in which anybody on that bank can ask her something and be answered for nothing.**
7. **A calendar note that Batch 0002 must carry:** the volume's Batch 0002 is the first week of the twelfth month of the year after to the fourth week of the second month of the year after, **which crosses a year boundary**, and the relative terms shift with it on the convention fixed above, so that in a twelfth-month scene *this year* is still the year after and *next year* is still the year after next, and a scene in the first or second month of the following stretch is the first week of a new year on the page while *this year* has not yet been re-based. **A Batch 0002 writer must state the convention it is using in its own closing section and must not leave it to be inferred.**

## THE INDEPENDENT REVIEW OF VOLUME 05 BATCH 0001, AND THE REPAIR THAT ANSWERED IT

**A review ran against Chapters 201–210 and its repair has been applied. This section is the authority for what the repair established and it is deliberately short. The review's own record, its eighteen findings, the two that were checked against the manuscript and found to be misreadings, and the two that were declined with their reasons, are in one place only: the closing section of `outline/batches/volume-05-batch-0001.md`, headed *The Independent Review Of This Batch, And The Repair That Answered It*. A writer who wants the detail reads that file and not this one. Nothing in the twenty-two-item record above has been restated here, and nothing in this section belongs anywhere else.**

**What the repair changed, in four rulings that a later writer must keep.**

1. **The asking is a person, and the count is a count of people. The rule is that a form cannot be asked and only a person can, and no form is ever asked anything.** An asking is one person asking another person what a word on a form means. **The count moves with the calendar and is one as at the second week of the ninth month, two from the first week of the tenth month, and three from the second week of the eleventh month. Three chapters of the batch had let a room or a form do the asking and three had given three different totals for the same century; all five are corrected on the page and in the four active state records.** A fourth asking, if a later batch writes one, is a person asking a person, out loud, in a room, about a word on a form, and every later total must say so and must agree with these three.
2. **Halla Wray's two sheets are two different objects and one of them is not in her hand.** The notice of six numbered lines, with the seal and nothing under it, has been on that bench since the seventh month. Her own copy of the six lines, in her own hand, with the day against it and no name on it, is in a book of her own. **Both are on the bench; only one is hers; neither has her name in it. A batch that says *two sheets of her own hand* is wrong, and a batch that says the count is one is also wrong.**
3. **Bess Tarrant has been unfindable for nine years and for no other span.** Chapter 0207 said sixty, which would have made her three. Nine is fixed by 0208 in three places and no chapter may give her another.
4. **The word counts are re-measured.** The batch is **28,790** and the manuscript is **739,525**; both were 28,624 and 739,359 when the writing run closed them, and the difference of 166 words is repair and not new writing. The ten chapters are 3,109 / 2,822 / 3,036 / 2,758 / 2,872 / 2,784 / 2,851 / 2,795 / 2,898 / 2,865.
