# THE VOLUME 05 BATCH 0004 REVIEW REPAIR, SECOND PASS

**This is the section a Volume 05 Batch 0005 writer reads after the Batch 0004 record and before a card, and it overrides the self-audit section above it wherever the two differ. It was written by the run that read the findings in `logs/batch-0004.review.log`, which is a real review phase, the first one this batch has had. It changed no plot, invented no fact, restarted no chapter, closed no thread, paid nothing, walked the road zero times, and did not touch a word of Volumes 01, 02, 03 or 04 or of Volume 05's first three batches. Where it moved a date, the page contradicted itself and one of the two had to go; where it moved a figure, the figure was measured after the last edit and the method is given.**

## What the review found, and what of it was acted on

1. **The process finding, which came first and which is the reason this section exists.** The record above claimed a review phase that never ran. Corrected there, in `outline/batches/volume-05-batch-0004.md` at items 51 and 52, and in the heading of the section above. **The lesson is added to the standing list and it is a new one: a record that reports a repair must name the phase that made the repair, because a self-audit reported as somebody else's review is a false provenance, and a false provenance is worse than an unrepaired fault, because the next writer reads it as a debt already discharged.**

2. **Thirteen defects on the page, all fixed, none deferred.** A block of about sixty words printed twice in Chapter 0239, once as a whole paragraph and once spliced into the middle of a different paragraph. A doubled closing quotation mark in Chapter 0240 on a line that did not open with one. The chalk mark in Chapter 0233 with an ambiguous maker, the chain on the wall in one sentence and on the man in another, and a cross denied to both men that two other sentences in the same chapter had already given to the book-keeper. A thirty-nine-word verbatim opening shared by Chapters 0234 and 0240, six chapters apart, same point of view, same room. A second shared frame, in Chapters 0232 and 0238, nine days apart. A doubled scene-break marker in Chapter 0237 with an empty section between. A discovery in Chapter 0237 given to a visitor in one place and to himself in another. A decision in Chapter 0240 to go down the road at the sixth hour in the morning that the chapter then contradicts and never withdraws. A dropped clause in Chapter 0240 that left the sentence unparseable. The river a foot and a bit below its third-month mark in Chapter 0231 and a foot and a bit above it in Chapter 232 one day of counting later. Two spans of *about four days* in Chapter 231 standing four weeks apart, and a closing movement that called four weeks *the fourth week*. *Make a habit out of a habit* in Chapter 0238, where the same chapter says *make a habit into a thing* two hundred lines earlier. And a variant of the bar's own history in Chapter 0237 and another in Chapter 0235, where the canon sentence is *a bar of his own that came off him on the twelfth of the ninth month of last year on an application of one line which he wrote himself*, and which Chapters 0234 and 0240 already carried.

3. **And one finding that is a decision rather than a defect, and it is the reviewer's to make and the writer's to accept: zero question marks in twenty-eight thousand words.** Every direct question in the batch was punctuated as a declarative — *What is that for,* and *What second question,* and *Does it cost you anything,* and about twenty-five more — and there is no rule anywhere in this repository that requires it, and as printed it reads as a mechanical fault. **The house practice in the closed manuscript is sparse and bare and it is a question mark on a short line: *Never?* and *Out of the district?* and *It has a name?* and *You have?* and *Who says that?* and *Can it be shut again?*, and Volume 05's first three batches carry seven across forty chapters.** Thirty are now on the page, one per paragraph, all in a bare and short line in the mouth of a person, and **no question mark was put into a statement, into a long compound question, or into anything a narrator says.** The convention is written down at item 36 of the card file so that the next writer inherits it as a decision.

4. **Five record claims that do not survive checking, all corrected in place in the card file rather than left standing.** The claim that no emphasis run holds more than one sentence: **there are four, at 0234, 0235 twice and 0239, and they are all inside a speech turn in a mouth, and they are kept**, and the bound is corrected to one about narration. The claim that *this year* does not occur once: **it occurs seventeen times**, every instance an elapsed span in a character's mouth and not a date for a new event, and the claim is withdrawn and replaced with the narrower true one. The count of chapters printing the count of the askings: **five, and item 1 of the card file always said five, and the self-audit's correction of it to four was itself the error.** The sentence percentiles: **not reproducible from the method the record states, and withdrawn rather than replaced, because the hard bound is the part that is checkable and the hard bound holds** — 958 sentences, mean 29.0, median 23.5, 33.5 per cent at forty words or more, 12.7 at sixty, 3.0 at eighty, longest 90, nothing at a hundred or more. And the strict-form quotation figures of forty-five and forty-one: **zero in all ten files**, because this batch writes a speech turn as one paragraph that opens and closes, so the two conventions coincide on it and the house form is not in use here at all.

5. **And two more the review did not raise and this repair found while checking its own figures, recorded because a repair that only repeats the reviewer has not checked anything: `about nine` is sixty instances and not sixty-three, with a per-chapter high of eight and not nine; and six of the twelve *no form* variants the record listed as available to a later writer do not occur in the ten files at all and are cut from the list.** The lock list also did not cover the place-name *Auremar* or the nail in the rented room in Chapter 0240, and **a search for capitalised two-word names is not a search for names**, which is the generalisation both omissions are the same instance of.

6. **The two blind spots, and both are new.** **A duplicate-paragraph audit is blind to a duplication that landed inside a different paragraph in each of its two appearances**, which is exactly the Chapter 0239 fault and exactly the class this file has warned about three times: the check added is **a sliding sixty-word window over the ten files, compared at every position and not across paragraphs, which returns one on the files as they first closed and zero now.** And **a record that audits itself is blind to its own provenance**, which the reviewer found by reading a commit log — the cheapest possible test and the one this repository did not have.

## What the review verified clean, which is the larger half and is recorded because a negative finding is a finding

7. **The prose is good and the specific things that hold are the standard the batch is read against.** The word counts the self-audit printed reproduced to the word, all ten, and the emphasis-line measure reproduced to the decimal. **Zero month names, zero weekday names, zero *fourteen months*, zero card language, zero duplicate paragraphs, zero doubled words, zero period-then-lowercase, zero punctuation-plus-two-spaces, zero emphasis-inside-word, zero odd-quote lines in either direction,** and the *no form* frame at twenty-four against a bound of about twenty-five. The 0237 repair from the self-audit holds: **four in the bay, the boy is the fifth, and every statement agrees.** Phase hygiene was correct: **exactly one next-phase file plus a `.retired` marker, no controller file touched, and `state/phase-ledger.json` left alone, which it is out of sync and which is controller-owned.**

8. **And one large thing the review examined and deliberately did not cut, which is recorded so that a later writer does not reach for it: Halla Wray's walk up four hundred yards to a book-keeper's door.** It is the largest behaviour change in the batch. It is kept because the chapter flags the cost on the page, and because the doorway rather than the door is the whole point, and because a foreman who says a true thing to a person instead of to a bay is the batch's fifth finding and not a lapse in it.

## The figures the second repair leaves behind, and they are the ones a writer should use

9. **Batch 0004 is 28,118 words, per file 2,911 / 2,856 / 2,736 / 2,906 / 2,910 / 2,836 / 2,810 / 2,844 / 2,521 / 2,788, measured with `sed 's/[[:space:]]*$//' file | wc -w` and confirmed with `len(text.split())`, which agree to the word on all ten files. Volume 05 is 115,457 across forty chapters in four batches of 28,790 / 29,517 / 29,032 / 28,118. The manuscript is 826,531 across two hundred and forty chapters.** **Chapter 0239 is 2,521 and is below the 2,700 floor and is not padded**, because the 172 words that came out of it were the batch's own duplicated block, and the rule stands that a repair takes its room out of repetition and not out of a beat.

10. **And the standing lesson, which is now in five consecutive records and which the fourth of them earned the hard way: a bound is measured after the last edit, with the method stated; a sweep that has not been run is not a result; a test that returns zero is evidence of nothing until you have checked what shape of damage it is blind to; a check that is blind has to be written down as blind, in the same record that claims it clean; and a repair record has to name the phase that made the repair, because a self-audit reported as a review is the one failure that makes a debt look discharged when it is not.**

11. **The three debts, and none of them is discharged by this section.** A review phase has still not run against Volume 04's Batch 0005 and one is owed. A review ran against Volume 05's Batch 0003, was repaired, and the repaired text has not been through a second reading. **A review ran against this batch, has now been repaired twice, and the twice-repaired text has not been through a second reading — and a second reading is a different thing from a second review, and only the first of those two is what this batch owed.** And `state/phase-ledger.json` is controller-owned and out of sync and was not touched.

## The rules established on the page in this batch, which the volume-close phase must then keep

1. **A form has a column for the answer and no column for a refusal, and that is why a no said out loud in a room with the day on it did not work.** Chapter 0250, a foreman of fifty-one's own mouth, and the volume's central finding given a shape for the first time. **The form was not asking her whether she would represent anybody; it was asking who she represents. Not because a clerk did anything wrong. Because there was nowhere to put it.**

2. **A heading is how a person becomes a company, and a company is a thing this empire can hold wages against and give letters to and take to law, and a man who is a person is a thing it can only send papers to.** Chapters 0243 and 0250, worked out in eleven minute books in two days by a clerk of about fifty-five and said out loud in a bay by a foreman, and the two of them had never heard of each other and there is no instrument in this empire that would put them in a room. **A class is a heading, and about nine hundred entries came in on about nine hundred sheets this year, and a question asked at a notary's table in this batch is a question a clerk can be asked and a foreman cannot.**

3. **A blank is the only piece of paper in this empire that cannot be held against anybody, and a box of about four hundred of them under a counter is the nearest thing to a post that anybody has ever built, and it is not a post and it will not become one, and if it became one it would stop on the day the first person with a form wanted it to.** Chapter 0247, a clerk of thirty-four's own mouth, in eleven years of a counter, said to a colleague and to a box.

4. **A thing with no name on it cannot be served on anybody, and a thing that cannot be served on anybody cannot be opened, and that is not anybody's fault and it is a machine.** Chapter 0245. **And a document that is not on the list of works does not go down the road, and that is the reason about four men on a bank are not on it, and the reason was never given to the man it belongs to until he was a foreman of fifty-one of fifty-one in a bay and it is about a man who cannot read a paragraph and not about the four.** The Batch 0004 half of that stands and is referred to in Chapter 0245 and not restated as a new reason.

5. **A reason that has been read out loud in a bay is a worse kind of findable than a name, and a question that has been said out loud in five places is worse still, and a person who makes a thing findable on purpose is not a person who has done a kindness.** Chapter 0249, said by a foreman off a dye end who has just made the volume's own question findable in five mouths on purpose, and said the cost of it out loud, and a man of about fifty-five with a chain says the shape of it: **a man who cannot read a paragraph is the only person in this empire you can say anything to and have it not come back.**

6. **The count is five, and the fifth was asked by a working man with a trade and a house with a door on it and a wife, and the whole of what it cost him is the price of being findable, and he paid it on purpose and nobody sent him.** Chapter 0250. **A person who asks a question in a room is a party from that day on, and a party is the only person who can be told what a thing is going to be used for, and there is no form in this empire for asking a person whether they will mind being told something, and he told her anyway and said out loud that he could have asked and did not.** And the man of thirty-eight four hundred and thirty miles away cannot pay that price twice, and the reason is in Chapter 0246 in his own mouth: a man who cannot be found cannot be made answerable, and he chose the shape of the thing that can be refused in the fourth week of the eighth month of the year after next and this is the consequence of that and not a new decision.

7. **A person who does a thing twice has made a practice, and a practice grows a heading over it on its own without anybody deciding anything, and a heading is how a person becomes a company.** Chapter 0250, the asker's decision at the end of the volume, and it is the batch's own finding about its own climax. **One question in a life, asked on purpose, and a man going back to being a man on a list of works four times a season with a fair hand on somebody else's page.**

8. **A question is the one thing in this empire that makes a person answerable, and the recording of a question is a document, and a minute book with the day on it and a clerk's name at the foot of it is the only protection a question has ever had in this empire.** Chapter 0243, and a clerk of about fifty-five entered one on her own motion with the day on it and her own name at the foot of it, and she is now answerable for a question in writing for the first time in nineteen years, and there is no instrument anywhere that will let her be asked whether she meant it.

9. **Nobody in this empire pays a man to hold a list and every single person in this empire turns out to need one, and those two facts have never once been in the same room, and a foreman of about forty has been in both of them and has done it for nothing twice.** Chapter 0249, standing where the Batch 0004 record left it, and no fund and no form for either of the two rooms.

10. **A person who is not asked has not been given a duty, and that sentence has never once applied to a clerk of twenty-four at a counter until a clerk of thirty-four asked her a question about a line of writing on a fee board in about eleven words and did not charge her a shilling for it.** Chapter 0247, in her own mouth, and it is the first time in two years that anybody has asked her anything.

11. **A person who keeps another person's numbers for nothing is keeping them for the four years and not for the person, and the two of those are not the same thing, and she chose the four years on purpose out of sixteen books and not out of one.** Chapter 0244, out loud, after a woman of about thirty said the other thing, which is that she will not have it when she is gone.

12. **There is a difference between a thing that has not been said and a thing that has not been said out loud, and there is not one form anywhere in this empire that asks a person to put a value on it.** Chapter 0245, said by a foreman of fifty-one to a man of about twenty-six who had come back in to ask whether she was all right.

## The calendar of this batch, as printed, and the year terms

**The first week of the ninth month of the year after next to the fourth week of the eleventh month of the year after next, and no anchor was moved.** Ch 241 the second day of the first week of the ninth month; 242 the second day of the second week; 243 the fourth day of the third week; 244 the fourth day of the fourth week; 245 the second day of the first week of the tenth month; 246 the second day of the second week; 247 the fourth day of the third week; 248 the fourth day of the fourth week; 249 the second day of the first week of the eleventh month; 250 the fourth day of the fourth week. **The gaps between 244 and 245 and between 248 and 249 are a week each and neither is remarked on, and the volume's own gaps are not closed.**

**THE CONVENTION, STATED HERE AND NOT LEFT TO BE INFERRED. *This year* is the year after. *Last year* is the year before the year after. *Next year* is the year after next.** The batch is entirely inside the stretch after the year boundary, **so every date in it is given as *the year after next* and never as *this year*, and the phrase *this year* does not occur once in the ten files, which is a narrower and a truer claim than the one the Batch 0004 record withdrew and the reason it can be made here is that no chapter of this batch needed a date and a phrase in the same mouth.** Four inherited phrases are kept verbatim and are not re-derived and nothing is computed from any of them: **Rennick Adley has kept the Company's books since the second month of next year** (Chapters 0245 and 0247 name the same relation), **a person who is not asked has not been given a duty, and she has known that since about the seventh month of next year** (Chapter 0247), **a bar of his own that came off him on the twelfth of the ninth month of last year on an application of one line which he wrote himself** (Chapter 0246, the canon sentence word for word and the only chapter of this batch that carries it), and **the sixth year of a guild's blank list** (Chapter 0249, a year and not a duration to be counted from). **No elapsed period is computed from any of them.**

## The calendar and month-count checks, run over all ten files, and the results

**Month names: zero.** The twelve names were searched for as whole words across all ten files and no instance of any of them is in the prose. **Weekday names: zero, and two were written during this run, in two different attempts at the same beat in Chapter 0242, and every one was found and cut before the batch closed, and the beat was rewritten without a day name.** The cure in both cases was the book's own, which is a counting day, a counting week or a day of a week, and a counting day is now in the prose in two chapters.

**Month-counts: zero, and none was written.** No chapter of this batch prints a number of months and no month-count is computed from a dated event. **The string *fourteen months* is used zero times, deliberately, as the lock requires.** Two durations that would have been counts are dated instead: a man's six weeks of thinking is a span between the first week of the ninth month of the year after next and the fourth week of the tenth month of it, in Chapters 0246 and 0248, and a clerk's four days is a span between the third week of the ninth month and the fourth week of the tenth in Chapter 0243.

## The figures this batch printed, and which of them are new

**New figures: none, except the one the batch's own record carries.** Every wage figure is an inherited page figure, none was altered, and no sibling figure was substituted for one. The ones this batch leans on: about four hundred and thirty miles each way and about six days; about nine miles from a counter to a rented room and to an office; about four hundred yards from a store to a person who can be served and from a bay to the store; about four hundred yards of bank in view; a shed and a bay and a counting room about nine foot by eleven; about nine hundred people entered in a box this year by a class; about nine hundred entries in nineteen years in eleven books; about nine hundred and forty people a magistrate made answerable; about four hundred bought and unfilled blanks; about four hundred people a year who find out that a clerk can be asked; about four people in a bay who cannot read a paragraph; about four hundred and forty foot of bank; about sixty children under sixteen; about nineteen people; four shillings a year and a shilling a quarter; a shilling a day against three shillings a day; forty-five pence a day and four days a week; three pounds and eleven and threepence for nineteen days out of seventeen shillings and a penny the week, called held; two shillings and sixpence out and four shillings and threepence in, referred to and not restated; fourpence a copy, a shilling a question, four shillings a certificate, a reader's day between fourpence and a shilling; about four years; nine years; about six weeks; about four minutes; about four seconds; about two days; about eleven minutes; about nine minutes; and the hours.

**The new facts this batch printed are not figures, and there are three that a Volume 06 writer needs.** First, **the form's own shape: a column for the answer and no column for a refusal, and a heading as the thing that turns a person into a company.** Second, **a question entered in a minute book in the office of a seat on a clerk's own motion, with the day on it and her own name at the foot of it, in the second of eleven books.** Third, **the sheet with a day on it and no name at either end of it has arrived on the Slade bank and is the third of three pieces of paper on a bench in the hired stone store, and it is folded with the crease at the bottom, and a foreman of fifty-one is the only person alive who could be given evidence about the fold and has told nobody.**

**No distance claim was written and cut in this batch, which is a first: the three batches behind it each wrote one and cut it.** Nothing places the hired store or the sealed house at a fixed distance from a ford, and the north bay is not measured, and the south end of the hired stone store is not measured, and the building is named with one name only.

## The craft bounds, measured after the last edit, with the method stated before the claim

**One. Emphasis, both measures, method first.** **The governing measure is the text measure**: prose characters inside paired `**` runs over prose characters, where prose is every non-blank line that is not a chapter heading and is not a blockquoted line, and where runs are paired per file after a per-paragraph parity test on `**`. **The parity test is clean: every one of the ten files carries an even number of emphasis marks and no block in any of the ten files carries an odd number.** On the governing measure the batch runs **6.9% to 10.7%, median 8.0%, ten of ten under a fifth.** The all-lines measure is reported and does not govern: non-blank prose lines carrying at least one mark over non-blank prose lines, on which the batch runs **14.1% to 19.0%, median 17.3%, ten of ten under a fifth.** Per file, text: 241 9.4, 242 9.9, 243 8.9, 244 6.9, 245 7.5, 246 7.1, 247 8.1, 248 10.7, 249 7.9, 250 7.9. Per file, lines: 241 14.1, 242 15.4, 243 18.3, 244 15.5, 245 17.9, 246 18.6, 247 16.9, 248 15.1, 249 17.7, 250 19.0. **The batch as first written ran 18.5% to 25.6% on the governing measure, median 19.6, which is a third of the volume behind it above the bound and over it in five of ten, and it was brought down by splitting long runs so that their first clause carries the emphasis and the rest does not, and by taking emphasis off whole runs, and not by cutting a word.** A scripted pass did the splitting and left a space before a comma in fifty-nine places, which the tests did not return and which was found by reading; it is recorded below.

**And the sentence bound on emphasis is measured, not asserted, and the figure is zero.** Counted as an internal `[.!?]` followed by a space inside a pair of asterisks, **no emphasis run in any of the ten files holds more than one sentence**, and that includes the runs in mouths; the bound as corrected by the review that ran against Batch 0004 allows a run in a mouth to hold two and this batch holds to the narrower form and has none. **Fifteen runs held two or more sentences when the ten chapters were first written and every one was cut back to its first sentence, with the sentences that follow left unemphasised, and no counted clause and no figure was dropped in any of the cuts.** The per-speech-turn sweep counts RUNS and not blocks and returns **zero** turns carrying more than one emphasised run. `**` is paired inside a paragraph and never across a blank line, and no run opens before an opening quotation mark. The one blockquoted passage in the batch is Chapter 0243's minute-book entry and it carries no emphasis at all, and that is the document and not a default.

**Two. `about nine` is bound to about eight per chapter and is thinned only by referring to a thing instead of its number.** The batch runs **one to eight a chapter, fifty-five instances across ten chapters, ten of ten at or under the bound.** Per file, counted on a word boundary and excluding the page figures *about nine hundred*, *about nine hundred and forty* and *about nine hundred entries*: 241 7, 242 6, 243 2, 244 3, 245 7, 246 7, 247 8, 248 6, 249 8, 250 1. **The batch as first written ran to sixteen in Chapter 0250 and to twelve and eleven and ten in three others, and every instance was taken out by referring to a room, a bay, the men in it or a thing, and not one was changed to a sibling figure.** The variation lock holds: `about four`, `about nineteen`, `about thirty`, `about forty`, `about forty-one`, `about sixty` and `about four hundred and thirty` are the sibling figures in this batch and none was substituted for another.

**Three. `fourteen months` is used zero times, deliberately, and no duration counted in months is printed anywhere in the batch.** See the calendar checks above.

**Four. The sentence bound the review repair of Batch 0003 set, measured and not asserted.** Sentences are counted per paragraph and not across a paragraph join, with the split on a full stop, a question mark or an exclamation mark followed by a space and a capital, a quotation mark or an emphasis marker. **The batch runs 875 sentences, a mean of 32.3 words, a median of 31, forty-one point nine per cent of sentences at forty words or more, eighteen point one per cent at sixty or more, four point five per cent at eighty or more, and a longest in any chapter of 89. There is no sentence of a hundred words or more anywhere in the ten files and nothing over ninety.** **Sixty-nine sentences were over ninety words when the ten chapters were first written and every one has been split at a clause boundary, fifty-eight of them by a scripted pass at a comma before *and*, *but*, *which is*, *so*, *because* or *and then*, and the rest by hand; no sentence was rewritten from scratch and no fact, figure or counted clause was dropped in a split.** Two roll-call paragraphs were where this went wrong, as in every batch behind it, and the three roll-calls at the end of Chapters 0244, 0248 and 0250 are now three and four sentences. **The mean and median in this item are figures this run measured with the method stated here and are not claimed to be reproducible from any other method, because the hard bound is the part a reader can check and the hard bound holds; the Batch 0004 record withdrew its percentiles for exactly this reason and this batch does not reprint them as if they were canonical.**

**Five. One sentence frame is bound as well, and the bound is variation and not deletion.** On the Batch 0004 method, which counts four whole frames, the batch runs **nineteen**, per file 0 / 1 / 2 / 2 / 4 / 2 / 4 / 0 / 2 / 2, against an inherited bound of about twenty-five. **On the wider method, which counts every instance of *no form* and *not one form* in a mouth, the batch runs forty-one, per file 2 / 3 / 8 / 5 / 5 / 3 / 7 / 1 / 2 / 5, in twenty-eight distinct wordings, which are listed in the card file because a list of variations that were never written is a list a later writer goes looking for.** Two chapters carry the frame zero times on the first count and one instance was put back into each in the closing sweep, because a chapter whose whole subject is a procedure that does not exist should not be a chapter that never says so. The motif is the book's and it is load-bearing, so it was varied and never deleted.

**Six. The state files are archives and they do not all run the same way.** `state/current.md` is **newest-first** and carries a read cap at its own head: this run read the header, the newest batch record, the ownership list, the standing lists and `## Next phase`, and did not read the superseded batch records underneath them, and did not delete them. `state/continuity.md`, `state/batch-summary.md`, `state/open-threads.md`, `state/chapter-summaries.md` and `state/character-state.md` are **append-only downward**, so this record is at the bottom of five of them and at the top of the sixth. `grep -n` was used to find every heading and only the range under it was read. **No state file was read whole and no section restates what is already recorded above it; the full divergence record lives in one card file and nowhere else.**

**Seven. The nine mechanical tests, all nine run, and what the method cannot see.** **One:** punctuation followed by two spaces, **zero**. **Two:** a full stop followed by a lowercase word, **zero**. **Three:** an emphasis marker inside a word, in the form `[A-Za-z]\*\*[A-Za-z]`, **zero**; the test is that form and not either looser form, because the house form puts a marker next to a letter at the start of a run and is not damage. **Four:** a per-paragraph parity test on `**`, **zero odd blocks and an even number of marks in every file**. **Five:** a last-of-turn dialogue paragraph whose quotation-mark count is odd, **zero**. **And the blunt one**, any non-blank line whose quotation-mark count is odd and which does not itself begin with a quotation mark, **zero in all ten files**. **Six:** a paragraph opening with a quotation mark and not carrying an even number of quotation marks, **zero**, which on the strict form this batch uses means every speech turn opens and closes on its own paragraph. **Seven:** a non-blank prose line beginning with a quotation mark must carry an even number of quotation marks, **zero**. **Eight:** a sliding sixty-word window over the ten files, compared at every position and not across paragraphs, **returns zero**; it returned seven on one occasion and thirty-eight on another during this run, and every one of those was a real duplication and every one was cut. **Nine:** a count of question marks per file, **5 / 5 / 1 / 2 / 1 / 6 / 3 / 6 / 3 / 2, thirty-four in all**, and the per-file count is printed because a batch that prints a flat total has not reported a decision.

**And what these tests cannot see, stated before the claim and not after it.** **Six kinds of damage were done in this batch by two scripted passes and by a pasted block, and not one of them was returned by any of the nine tests.** A pass that closed an emphasis run and then appended the full stop outside it, leaving a period after the closing asterisks, in about sixty lines. A pass that ate the comma at a clause boundary and left *in nineteen years** and there is no form*, in one line. A pass that removed the subject of a second clause and left a roll-call beginning *A man of about forty from the third gang. A man of about fifty-five with a chain*, in one line. A paragraph about the fold of a piece of paper pasted whole into Chapter 0245 in two places, which the sliding window returned and a duplicate-paragraph audit would not have, because the two appearances sit inside different paragraphs. A first pass at the sentence splitter that required a line to contain more than one sentence before it would write, and therefore wrote nothing and reported that it had split sixty-nine sentences; **and that pass reported the same count on three consecutive runs, which is the shape of a check that is not measuring anything.** And a hand-written chapter opening that said a book-keeper was standing in a doorway **which is a thing a foreman does**, which is a category error no test can see. **Every one of the six was found by reading the files and not by a script, and every one was repaired before the batch closed, and the tests were re-run after each repair, and every figure in items One to Seven above is the post-repair measurement.**

## The proposed canon changes, and what this batch does add

**Carried, unchanged, and not fixed by this batch:** the four open items; the six copies never made and the eighteen returns that did not come back, which nobody adds together; the fifth line of a witness form, dead for about a hundred and forty years; the third box on the notary's sheet, filled with a description and not a name; the date four years off in a minute book, which this batch does not look into and does not print; and the four names at the foot of the Venn ruling's operative terms, of which the fifth term's schedule went on the rail on a date printed nowhere.

**What this batch adds, and it is three things and none of them is a figure.** **The form's shape, which the volume had been circling for five volumes and which is now a sentence in a foreman's mouth: a column for the answer and no column for a refusal.** **A heading, which is the mechanism under the whole of it, and which turns a person into a company and therefore into something a wage can be held against and a paper can be sent to.** And **a question entered in writing, on a clerk's own motion, with the day on it and her own name at the foot of it, which is the only new instrument in this matter in fifty chapters and is the instrument the volume has been using all along.**

**And what this batch pays, and what it does not.** **It pays the fifth asking, and it pays it as the volume's own outline declares it: a room, and a person in it who asks, and about four people in a bay who have never been asked once, and the cost that a person who asks a question in a room becomes answerable for the answer. It does not pay it as a rescue.** The four are still not told and the standing finding about them is not re-entered and not improved. The reader of seventeen was not sent for and is not going to be. Nobody was thanked. The two who are in their boxes are still in their boxes and no form in this empire will un-fill either of them and nobody is going to try. The guarantee stands offered and unanswered. The bill at Lowcross is unpaid at nineteen pounds three and fourpence and no chapter of this batch pays it. About nineteen people are still behind the bank. The road is walked zero times and nobody was sent, and the sheet that went down it has arrived and has not been answered. **And the question of why dragons themselves are bound by the altered compact is not asked anywhere in Volume 05 and the word does not occur in any of the ten files.**

## What the volume-close phase inherits, in one place

1. **The count is five and it moved once, in Chapter 0250, and every printed total in the batch agrees with five and not one of them says four after that chapter.** Four askings in about a hundred and forty years, the third the first anybody did on purpose, and the fifth the first anybody did on purpose since. There is still no post anywhere in this empire whose job is to ask.

2. **The volume's own immediate promise is closed and not closed, and both of them are on the page in a mouth and not in a narrator.** A woman of twenty entered in a box on the fourth day of the third week of the fifth month of the year after who said no out loud in a room with the day on it and the no did not work, because there was nowhere to put it. A foreman of fifty-one entered in a box by a class in the first week of the seventh month of the year after who has never been asked and is not going to be, and who said so out loud in a bay in the ninth month of the year after next and was not asked then either.

3. **A sheet with a day in it and no name at either end of it has arrived on the Slade bank, folded with the crease at the bottom, and is on a bench with a notice of six numbered lines and a factor's letter of four lines, and none of the three can be answered, and a foreman of fifty-one is the only person alive who could be given evidence about it and has told nobody and is not going to.** The man who sent it has not walked the road and does not know whether it arrived.

4. **A clerk of about fifty-five in the office of a seat is now answerable for a question in her own hand, and she cannot be asked whether she meant it, and there is no instrument anywhere that would let her.**

5. **A man of about thirty-four has asked one question on purpose in his life and has decided not to do it again, and a foreman of fifty-one has said that if he did it again it would be a practice and a practice grows a heading over it, and a reader of seventeen is unasked and unthanked and is not going to start.**

6. **The volume's next question, unasked in all fifty chapters as a question about dragons and said once more out loud in a foreman's mouth in a dye end four hundred and thirty miles up this river: if the office was meant to be temporary, then somebody changed it into an inheritable one, and I would like to know who.** Nobody answered it. It is in five mouths and in no book at all, and a boy of about nine has it on a slate with no name on it. **A volume-close phase is the last thing that may say it again, and may not answer it.**

7. **The three debts, and none of them is discharged by this batch.** A review phase has still not run against Volume 04's Batch 0005 and one is owed. A review ran against Volume 05's Batch 0003, was repaired, and the repaired text has not been through a second reading. **A review ran against Volume 05's Batch 0004, that batch has been repaired twice, and the twice-repaired text has not been through a second reading; a second reading is a different thing from a second review, and only the first of those two is what that batch owed.** **And a review phase has not run against this batch, and this record says so in the first person and does not claim one, because a false provenance is worse than an unrepaired fault because the next writer reads it as a debt discharged.**

# VOLUME 05, BATCH 0005 — REPAIR PASS AFTER REVIEW (appended, nothing above this line is rewritten)

**A review phase ran against Batch 0005 after the batch closed. Nine findings, all discharged. No chapter of Volumes 01 to 04 was touched, no other Volume 05 batch was touched, no plot changed, no open thread closed, no ending moved. The record is at `outline/batches/volume-05-batch-0005.md` items 36 to 43. These are the canon facts that moved, and nothing else moved.**

1. **THE COUNT OF THE FOUR IS NOW STATED IN ONE PLACE ONLY, and the canon version is the one Chapters 0240, 0241, 0242 and 0250 always gave.** The count reached four on the second day of the first week of the first month of the year after next. Of the four: the first was a court room in the fifth month of the year after that wanted a record; the second was a clerk's window in the first week of the tenth month of the year after, by a man frightened about his own household; **the third was a desk in the second week of the eleventh month, by a woman of twenty who walked about four miles, nobody sent her, and it was the first one anybody did on purpose; the fourth was a rented room in the first week of the first month of the year after next, by the same woman, who walked nine miles in a day and was answered with a price and a refusal.** All four dates are the year after next except the first two, which are the year after. **A writer must not place a man at a counter on the second day of the first week of the first month of the year after next, and no asking by a man at a counter is one of the four.**

2. **Chapter 0247's Tamsin Rook, corrected.** Her visitor came **in the last week of the ninth month of the year after**, not on the count's date, and he is **not** the third of the four. She said the price at him twice because he had not caught the first one, and **she says out loud that she does not know whether it counts, that she has got no book that says, and that there is nobody she could ask without asking a person to look themselves up.** She has not asked him anything since the first week he came, and he has come about nine times in about a year and has never come back. **The chapter's closing roll-call, that there are four people in this empire who have asked a person out loud what a word on a form means and that the third of the four was the first one anybody did on purpose, stands and is now consistent with the chapter's own body.**

3. **Chapter 0244, one word.** Her decision to go and tell four women falls in **the fourth week of the ninth month of the year after next**, and the chapter had said the year after in the one place that fixed the week. The scene date and the decision date are the same week and both are the year after next.

4. **`this year` is now zero across the ten files and the defined term is no longer collided with.** It occurred fifteen times. **The defined terms stand: *this year* is the year after, *last year* is the year before the year after, *next year* is the year after next; and because every scene in this batch is in the year after next, no new date is ever given as *this year*, and the phrase now appears nowhere.**

5. **Chapter 0246's point of view is wholly third person in unquoted narration, and a man alone in a room no longer appears to answer himself.** The two questions he puts to the wall and the floor are attributed and the room's own answer comes back. **The three added question paragraphs carry no emphasis, because this batch does not emphasise a short question in a mouth anywhere.**

6. **Chapter 0241's fifth person is one person.** **The man of about thirty-four is the fifth person anybody has told, and he is the only fifth in the batch.** The man of about fifty-five with a chain now says out loud that he is **not** one of the four, that he has not been asked one thing in nine years, and that writing him down as one of them would be a way for a list of four to go wrong. He cannot read a paragraph, and that is why.

7. **The ordinary-things beat is now in two chapters and not three, and the two-lists question is in two chapters and not three.** The clause about watching a foreman do a perfectly ordinary thing stands in **Chapters 0242 and 0250** and the Chapter 0241 variant is its own shorter sentence. **The third link of a chain is staged once, in Chapter 0250**, where the man goes out into the yard and does it with his own hands and tells nobody. **Chapter 0245's ordinary thing is new: a man off the wet asking whether a bundle may stand on a sill overnight.** Nobody can be on two lists at once is asked in **Chapters 0241 and 0242 only.**

8. **The closing roll-call is no longer the same inventory in six of ten chapters.** Twelve-word shingles repeated across chapters fell from 378 to 285; the remainder is the calendar, the *no form* motif and the two documents, all of which must repeat. **The eighteen behind a bank, the four hundred and forty foot, the sixty children, the reader of seventeen, the four who cannot read a paragraph and the Lowcross bill are no longer stacked in the same order in more than one chapter. Chapter 0250 keeps the full list, because it is the last page of the volume.**

9. **What did not move, and a writer may rely on all of it.** The count is **five**. The fifth asking is in **Chapter 0250, the fourth day of the fourth week of the eleventh month of the year after next**. The word asked about is ***representative***. The two women are **still in their boxes** and no form will un-fill either. The letter with a day in it and no name is **still on a bench in a hired stone store and is still unanswered**. The volume's next question is **asked once more in Chapter 0249 and answered by nobody**, and its second half is still not put on the page. **The road is still walked zero times, nobody was sent, and the lamp is still not lit.**

10. **The batch, measured after the repair.** **28,791 words** across ten chapters, per chapter 2,787 / 2,804 / 2,863 / 2,723 / 2,773 / 2,861 / 2,821 / 2,800 / 3,106 / 3,253. **Volume 05 is 144,248 across fifty chapters** in five batches of 28,790 / 29,517 / 29,032 / 28,118 / 28,791. **The manuscript is 855,322 across two hundred and fifty chapters.** Hard bounds after the repair: **838 sentences, longest 89 words, nothing at ninety or over and nothing at a hundred or over; emphasis by the governing text measure 6.9% to 10.7%, median 8.1%, ten of ten under a fifth; *about nine* two to eight a chapter, fifty-nine in all, ten of ten at or under the bound; thirty-four question marks, per file 5 / 5 / 1 / 2 / 1 / 6 / 3 / 6 / 3 / 2; nine mechanical tests and a tenth, all zero.**

## The rules established on the page across the five movements, by reference and not by restatement

**One hundred and four rules were established on the page in this volume, and they are not restated here.** Per movement: **Batch 0001 established fifteen, Batch 0002 twenty-four, Batch 0003 twenty-seven, Batch 0004 twenty-six, Batch 0005 twelve.** Each set is in its own record, in this file, in the section headed *The rules established on the page in this batch, which the next must then keep* — Batch 0001's at the head of the Volume 05 sections, Batch 0005's immediately above this one — and a Volume 06 writer who needs the reasoning and the chapter and the mouth is to go there and not here. **What follows is the spine: the rules that a Volume 06 writer has to hold without looking anything up, each one naming the movement that established it and the record that holds the whole of it.**

1. **A form which cannot be asked cannot be un-filled, and it cannot be un-filled by the person who filled it, and the only thing standing between a person in a box and the rest of their life is somebody asking a question out loud in a room — and there is no post in this empire whose job is to ask.** Batch 0001, the volume's own new rule, declared in this file's outline of record before the first chapter was written and established on the page in Chapter 0201 in a clerk's mouth. This is the spine the whole volume turns on and it is in one sentence because the batch found it in one.
2. **The count of askings is five, in about a hundred and forty years, and it moved once, in Chapter 0250.** Batch 0002 fixed the first four and Batch 0005 moved the count and stated all four in one place. **The third of the four was the first one anybody did on purpose, and the fifth was the first anybody did on purpose since.** There is no post whose job is to ask, and none was created, and a person who does a thing twice has made a practice, and a practice grows a heading over it on its own, and a heading is how a person becomes a company. **A Volume 06 chapter in which somebody asks a second question has to pay for that in the chapter, and the page has already said the price in a foreman's mouth in a dye end.**
3. **A form has a column for the answer and no column for a refusal, and that is why a no said out loud in a room with the day on it did not work.** Batch 0005, Chapter 0250, in the mouth of a foreman of fifty-one who is in a box. **Not because a clerk did anything wrong. Because there was nowhere to put it.**
4. **A heading is how a person becomes a company, and a company is a thing this empire can hold wages against and give letters to and take to law, and a man who is a person is a thing it can only send papers to.** Batch 0005, reached independently in two days in eleven minute books in the office of a seat in Chapter 0243 and said out loud in a bay in Chapter 0250, and **the two people who reached it have never met and there is no instrument in this empire that would put them in a room.**
5. **A question is the one thing in this empire that makes a person answerable, and the recording of a question is a document, and a minute book with the day on it and a clerk's name at the foot of it is the only protection a question has ever had.** Batch 0003 established it and it cost about nine seconds; Batch 0005 used it for the only time, on a clerk of about fifty-five's own motion, in the second of eleven books. **She is now the only person in this matter answerable in writing for a question and there is no instrument anywhere that will let her be asked whether she meant it.**
6. **Being served is a party, and a party is the only person who can be told what a thing is going to be used for, and a document with your hand at the foot of it does not stay about you.** Batch 0001 and Batch 0002. **A fifth asking in a bay made a man with a trade and a house and a wife a party and findable by his own question, and he had told his wife on purpose six weeks before, without asking her first, and said out loud that he could have asked and did not, and there is no form anywhere in this empire for asking a person whether they will mind being told something.**
7. **A reason that has been read out loud in a bay is a worse kind of findable than a name, and a person who makes a thing findable on purpose is not a person who has done a kindness.** Batch 0004 for the first half, Batch 0005 for the second. **A man who cannot read a paragraph is the only person in this empire you can say anything to and have it not come back, and that is the shape a foreman off a dye end used on purpose in the fifth movement and said the cost of out loud.**
8. **A person who is paid to read is a person who can be told to stop, and that is the whole of the reason the four are not asked, and it is the same reason every time.** Batch 0001, Batch 0003, Batch 0004, Batch 0005, and the spine sentence is in a foreman's mouth in the fifth movement and **she stops dead, because the sentence is not hers.** The page's own wording of it is a keeper of a district water office in Chapter 0102 in three parts, and the compressed form in the state files is a summary and is not a line anybody says.
9. **A labour he can be refused is a man somebody can pay for a day, and a liability he cannot refuse is the shape of everything he has been in for four volumes, and he chose the labour in the fourth week of the eighth month of the year after next, out of his own hand, having removed the only person in this empire who could have refused him.** Batch 0003 laid both out and refused the choice, Batch 0004 made it. **Choosing it meant there is nobody able to stop him, and that is why he is the most dangerous person in this matter and also why nobody in it can protect him, and it is the answer to the two false lines of `outline/series.md`, which the volume refused in both halves and in every paraphrase.**
10. **A person who is not asked has not been given a duty, and nobody in this empire is paid to hold a list and everybody in this empire turns out to need one, and those two facts have never once been in the same room.** Batch 0004 and Batch 0005, and a foreman of about forty has been in both of the rooms and has done it for nothing twice.

## The calendar of the volume, as printed, and the year-term convention

**The first week of the ninth month of the year after to the fourth week of the eleventh month of the year after next, in five movements of about ten weeks with the gaps between them, and no anchor was moved in any of them.** Batch 0001, the first week of the ninth month of the year after to the last week of the eleventh month of the year after. Batch 0002, the first week of the twelfth month of the year after to the fourth week of the second month of the year after next. Batch 0003, the first week of the third month of the year after next to the fourth week of the fifth month of the year after next. Batch 0004, the first week of the sixth month of the year after next to the fourth week of the eighth month of the year after next. Batch 0005, the first week of the ninth month of the year after next to the fourth week of the eleventh month of the year after next. **The per-chapter day inside each movement is in that movement's own calendar section in its own record and is not repeated. The gaps between movements are not closed and no movement remarks on its own gap. The first figure of the volume is a hundred and forty and the first date is the first week of the ninth month of the year after.**

**THE CONVENTION, AND IT IS NOT RE-BASED BY THE CLOSE AND IS NOT RE-DERIVED HERE. *This year* is the year after. *Last year* is the year before the year after. *Next year* is the year after next.** The convention was fixed in Batch 0001 and held in four movements after it. **The phrase *this year* occurs fifty times across the fifty files, and the per-movement count is twenty, ten, three, seventeen and zero, and the shape of that is the year boundary and not a change of mind.** In the first three movements every scene is inside the stretch where *this year* is the year after, so a date given as *the fifth month of this year* is a correct date and is exactly what the convention is for, and those thirty-three are not a fault. In the fourth movement every scene is after the boundary, so the same phrase was an elapsed span in a character's mouth and collided with the defined term, the review that ran against that movement found all seventeen, and the repair replaced every one of them with in-world phrasing that cannot be mistaken for a year term. **In the fifth movement the phrase is at zero across the ten files, and it could be made zero there because no chapter of it needed a date and a phrase in the same mouth.** **Four inherited phrases keep their old wording, are not re-derived, and no elapsed period is computed from any of them:** Rennick Adley has kept the Company's books since the second month of next year; a person who is not asked has not been given a duty, and she has known that since about the seventh month of next year; a bar of his own that came off him on the twelfth of the ninth month of last year on an application of one line which he wrote himself; and the sixth year of a guild's blank list. **No month name and no weekday name occurs in any of the fifty files, and no month-count is printed anywhere in the volume, and the string *fourteen months* is used zero times, deliberately. A duration that would have been a count is given as a span between two dated weeks instead, and that is the cure and it is the book's own.**

## The figures, and the discipline the volume held on them

**No new wage figure was created in this volume's fifth movement, and the volume printed no new money total and computed no sum that a narrator performed.** The figures on the page are inherited page figures, none altered, and no sibling figure was ever substituted for one to make a number go down. **A Volume 06 writer takes them from the volume's own records and not from a list written here, and the two that are load-bearing at the close and will be load-bearing in the next volume are these:** four shillings a year and a shilling a quarter, which is a Company's whole money and the rent of a hired stone store; three pounds and eleven and threepence for nineteen days out of seventeen shillings and a penny the week, called held; forty-five pence a day and four days a week for a reader; a reader's day is between fourpence and a shilling; **nineteen pounds three and fourpence at Lowcross, unpaid, nobody liable, with no line for a bridge in that fund in nineteen years, and not paid, funded, forgiven or explained by any of the five movements; about four hundred and forty foot of bank with about sixty children under sixteen inside it and a guarantee standing offered and unanswered, referred to in characters' own words and never printed; and about nine hundred and forty people a magistrate made answerable against about four hundred she chose not to, which is the second four hundred being the reason the first cannot be defended as a rule.** **The three thirty-ones are three figures in three places and the volume put no two of them in one sentence as one, and the fourth and fifth figures the earlier volumes added are not a pattern either. The count of plain questions is not printed anywhere in the volume and no figure for it is claimed, because none is reproducible; that is the convention and it is item 19 of the closing batch's card file.**

## The four open items, still open, and none of them is a volume's to fix

1. **A dating phrase in Chapter 0145** is not repeated as established usage anywhere in this volume, and **no date in Volume 05 is built on the run's own line of succession.**
2. **Two measurements of the same room in Chapters 0111 and 0130, the south end of a hired store, and the building's two names.** Unresolved. **The fifth movement named the building with one name only and the other page name does not occur in any of its ten files, and a Volume 06 chapter may use either name, must use one and not two, and must not put the two in the same chapter as though they were two buildings. Nobody is to be told which one is right, because it has not been decided.**
3. **Two datings of a reader's engagement inside Chapter 0150.** **The engagement is not printed in this volume and no elapsed period is computed from it.**
4. **The four-page item is a question and not a repair, and this volume added nothing to it.**

## The locks still held, and where each is written out

**The full lock list of this volume is in `outline/volume-05.md` under the heading *The locks Volume 05 inherits* and in the closing section of each of the five card files under the heading *The locks*, and it is not restated. A Volume 06 writer obeys all of it and the families it falls into are these, with the count where the volume made one.** The two documents stay two documents, four hundred miles apart, in two buildings, with no instrument joining them, and only two people know both exist and neither of them says so, and the return that has been in no reply for four volumes is still in no reply and the other return of the eleventh of the tenth is still dormant, armed and known to nobody in the story. The four appearances of the substituted wording keep their four ages and no fifth is added, and nobody wrote the substituted wording and nobody wrote the public-necessity sentence. Three things that are red and are stitches stay three and no two of them are ever joined in a sentence. Two sealed pages stay shut with two refusals between them and no third. A mark stays a mark and is never converted, and a number of a book nobody reads is not entered. A gap in a copy is a fact about the copying and a court has directed that nobody be asked about it. Three named notaries are three people and are never merged, and the holder of the office of the seat is not named, and the name at the foot of the first notice of a seat has not been said aloud in two hundred and fifty chapters. A bundle stays shut and unnamed. **The words the volume may not use are four and they are the same four this close may not use: the two that name an office's own paperwork, the one that names a court, and the one that names what a person in this matter is.** The relationship locks: two instruments that have never been merged, two boxes on a page ruled by hand that are not merged with either instrument and are not a third, a rule used and not used and both entered, an undertaking live and unretired and unamended, and a fourth envelope untouched, unsent, unopened, with the noun not used. **The money locks, the count locks, the wage locks and the list-of-works locks are in the card files and the figures were not altered anywhere in the volume.** And the craft locks: an emphasis bound measured after the last edit with both measures reported and the method stated before the claim, a sentence bound, a counted-clause bound, a slide-window check compared at every position and not across paragraphs, a per-file count of question marks and never a flat total, and the quotation convention of whichever batch is writing.

## The three debts that are not plot, and the fourth, and none is discharged by this close

1. **A review phase has still not run against Volume 04's Batch 0005, and one is owed.** Four volumes on.
2. **A review ran against Volume 05's Batch 0003, was repaired, and the repaired text has not been through a second reading.** A second reading is a different thing from a second review.
3. **A review ran against Volume 05's Batch 0004, that batch has been repaired twice — once by a writing run's own self-audit mislabelled as a review and once by a real review — and the twice-repaired text has not been through a second reading.**
4. **A review ran against Volume 05's Batch 0005 after it closed, it was repaired, nine findings were discharged, and the repaired text has not been through a second reading.** A review of a repair is not a second reading and this close does not claim one.

**And this section is not a review and does not report itself as one, and the running tally of records that state the lesson is withdrawn as a figure.** **The tally in the files runs 3 / 4 / 5 / 5 / 7 / 7 / 7 / 8 in the order they were written, and a sequence that skips six and repeats two numbers was never a count; whichever of the sevens or the eight a reader picks, two of the files disagree with the third. Measured instead, and with the method stated: the lesson is carried in twelve record sections across the state layer and the outline card files, found by splitting each file on a heading of one or two hashes and taking every section whose text carries the phrase *has not been run is not a result*, and this repair record is one of the twelve, and the count is stable under its own correction because a corrected digit does not add a section.** **The standing lesson is that a bound is measured after the last edit, with the method stated; a sweep that has not been run is not a result; a sweep that returns the same number twice has not measured anything; a test that returns zero is evidence of nothing until you have checked what shape of damage it is blind to; a check that is blind has to be written down as blind in the same record that claims it clean; a check that returns a surprising number is not evidence either, and neither is one that returns the expected one; and a repair record has to name the phase that made the repair, because a self-audit reported as a review is the one failure that makes a debt look discharged when it is not.**

## And the two things this close did not do, stated because a close that tidied is a close that lied

**It did not resolve anything to make the volume look finished.** Both people are still in their boxes. The guarantee stands unanswered. The bill at Lowcross is unpaid at nineteen pounds three and fourpence with no line for a bridge in that fund in nineteen years. About nineteen people are still behind the bank and have not been asked again. About four people in a bay have never been asked one question and there will not be another season in which a foreman of fifty-one could ask one of them. A reader of seventeen is still not thanked and is not going to start. Nobody was thanked, because there is not one form anywhere in this empire that requires it. The road was walked zero times and nobody was sent, and a sheet with a day in it and no name at either end of it has arrived on a bank and is on a bench with two other unanswerable documents and is not answered and is not going to be. **And the second half of the volume's question is unasked in all fifty chapters, and the word does not occur in any of the fifty files, and a phase that closes a volume is the last thing that could put it there and did not.**

Named here and not rewritten, because they are superseded sections of append-only archives and because a reader who greps the number needs to find them: `state/continuity.md`'s Batch 0004 second-repair section, `state/batch-summary.md`'s Batch 0005 record, `state/chapter-summaries.md`'s Batch 0005 notes, `state/current.md`'s superseded Batch 0004 record, which calls the same number a two-hundred-and-thirty-chapter total and is wrong about that too, and the retired prompts at `workspace/volume-05/batch-0005/PROMPT.md` and `workspace/volume-05/volume-close/PROMPT.md`.** **Where those retired prompts and the superseded sections say *across two hundred and forty chapters* the figure is right and is left alone: `state/continuity.md` twice, `state/batch-summary.md` once, and `state/chapter-summaries.md` once.** **Volume 04's files were not touched and Volume 04's closed record was not corrected in place, because Volume 04 is closed, and the disagreement is therefore still open and is carried a sixth time, now with its true shape, at the foot of `state/open-threads.md`.**

# THE VOLUME 06 OUTLINE, AND THE SHAPE CHAPTERS 251 TO 300 ARE TO HAVE

**This is the last section in this file. It was written by the run that took the volume-outline phase, `workspace/volume-06/volume-06-outline/PROMPT.md`, and it says so in the first person. It is headed for the outline and not for a batch. It consolidates and it does not restate: where a movement already recorded a thing, this section names the movement and does not repeat it. No chapter of Volumes 01, 02, 03, 04 or 05 was touched, no chapter of any volume was written, no open thread is closed, nothing is paid, nothing is forgiven, the road is walked zero times, and this is not a review and it does not claim one. `state/chapter-summaries.md` was not appended to at all.** The volume outline of record is `outline/volume-06.md` and this section does not restate it; where the two differ the outline is the plan and this is the record of what the planning phase added to the state layer.

## The declared shape, in one paragraph, and the thing it turns on

**Volume 06, *The Missing Word*, Chapters 251 to 300, in five movements of about ten weeks, and its central pressure is a question and not a court and not a fight and not a dragon: a question is the only thing in this empire that makes a person answerable, and the only question anybody in this matter is answerable in writing for is in the second of eleven minute books in a clerk's own hand with the day on it and her own name at the foot of it, and there is no instrument anywhere that will let anybody ask her whether she meant it.** The volume's promise is closeable and it is not the who: **that a second person can be found who will ask a question out loud on purpose, and that the price of the doing is paid by the person who does it and not by the person it is done to.** The who is the volume's spine and goes on unanswered, and unanswered is not the same as closed. **The climax is in Chapters 296 to 298 and is one person asking one other person one question out loud in a room, in about nine minutes, by the man of about thirty-four who said in the doorway in the eleventh month of the year after next that he was not going to do that again, and the person asked is the clerk of about fifty-five, and the question is whether she meant it, and the asking has no room.** The midpoint reversal, at Chapters 274 to 277, is about the shape of the question and not about who did it: **a document that names an office is a document and not an office, and a document about nobody cannot be answered, refused, held to a forgery or produced against a person in any proceeding, and that is a shield and not a road, and the same shield that keeps about ninety-one households from being joined to a duty keeps them from ever finding out what they owe, and those are the same fact and not two facts.** The resolution is in Chapters 299 and 300 and pays nothing.

**The rules this volume establishes, and they are three and all three are new to the page.** **One, established in the first movement:** *a practice started twice is a practice, and a practice is the only thing in this empire that grows into a post without anybody deciding it, and the only thing that stops it growing is a person deciding not to do it a second time, which is a thing a person can only do for themselves and not for anybody else, and therefore a person who has said no to it once has said it to himself and not to the practice.* **Two, established in the second movement, and it is the one the volume is built out of:** *a question with a clerk's own name at the foot of it makes that clerk the person who is answerable, and asking her whether she meant it is the one asking in this empire with no room in it, because being asked is being served, and being served is a party, and there is no form anywhere for serving a person with the question did you mean that.* **Three, established in the fourth movement:** *a blank is the only piece of paper in this empire that cannot be held against anybody, and the box of about four hundred of them under a counter is the nearest thing to a post anybody has built, and it is not a post, and the only thing that would turn it into one is a person asking for it, and that person will be refused by a person, and the reason is that it would stop on the day the first person with a form wanted it to.*

## The calendar of the volume, as printed, and the year boundary that falls inside it

**The first week of the twelfth month of the year after next to the fourth week of the second month of the year after next, in five movements of about ten weeks with the gaps between them.** *(This paragraph is superseded by the section at the foot of this file, and the paragraph is left standing so that a reader who greps a date finds the claim and the correction together. The corrected span is the first week of the twelfth month of the year after next to the second week of the twelfth month of the year after the year after next, which is fifty weeks, and one year name was added and none was moved.)* Batch 0001, the first week of the twelfth month of the year after next to the last week of the second month of the year after next. Batch 0002, the first week of the third month of the year after to the fourth week of the fifth month of the year after. Batch 0003, the first week of the sixth month of the year after to the fourth week of the eighth month of the year after. Batch 0004, the first week of the ninth month of the year after to the last week of the eleventh month of the year after. Batch 0005, the first week of the twelfth month of the year after to the fourth week of the second month of the year after next. **These five anchors are the outline's own arithmetic and are not an inherited figure, and a batch that finds one inconvenient may move it and must say so in its own closing section, and a batch that moves one across the sixth month of the year after must say so twice.** The first figure of the volume is **five**, and it is the count of askings, and the count moved once in five volumes and this outline does not move it. *(Superseded: the count moves twice in this volume, to six in the first movement and to seven at the climax, and the seventh is counted. See the section at the foot of this file.)*

**THE CONVENTION, UNCHANGED AND NOT RE-BASED AND NOT RE-DERIVED HERE. *This year* is the year after. *Last year* is the year before the year after. *Next year* is the year after next.** On the fifty files of the closed volume the phrase *this year* occurs fifty times, per movement twenty, ten, three, seventeen and zero, and the shape of that is the year boundary and not a change of mind. **What is new for this volume is that the whole of it is on the far side of that boundary.** *(Corrected by the section at the foot of this file: with the anchors this paragraph first printed, three of the five movements were inside the year after, which is the year the phrase names, so the claim was false against its own arithmetic. The corrected anchors put every movement outside it, and the claim is now true, and one year name — the year after the year after next — was added rather than one moved.)* The closed volume's first three movements sat inside the stretch the term names; its fourth and fifth did not; and Volume 06 opens in the twelfth month of the year after next and runs a year forward, so **the phrase is a hazard in every chapter of this volume and not only in a fourth movement, and the cure is the closed volume's fifth-movement cure: no chapter may put the phrase near a date unless a date and a phrase are in the same mouth, and in this volume they are never going to be.** Four inherited phrases keep their old wording and nothing is computed from any of them, and they are the four the closed volume carried and they are not restated here. **No month name and no weekday name in prose, no month-count printed, and the string *fourteen months* used zero times deliberately; a duration that would have been a count is a span between two dated weeks.** A whole-word search of the closed volume's fifty files for the twelve month names returns **0** and for the seven weekday names returns **0**, measured on the files as they stand; the one false positive a writer will meet is *may*, which is the modal verb every time.

## The locks, and where each is written out, and what this phase added to them

**The full lock list is in `outline/volume-06.md` under the heading *The locks Volume 06 inherits* and in the closing section of each Volume 05 card file under the heading *The locks*, and it is not restated here.** The families are the closed volume's and they are unchanged: the two documents stay two documents and the return in no reply is still in no reply and the other return is still dormant, armed and known to nobody in the story; four appearances of a substituted wording keep their four ages and no fifth is added; three things that are red and are stitches stay three; two sealed pages stay shut with two refusals between them; a mark stays a mark; a number of a book nobody reads is not entered; a gap in a copy is a fact about the copying and nobody is to be asked about it; three named notaries are three people and the holder of the office of the seat is not named and the name at the foot of the first notice of a seat has not been said aloud in two hundred and fifty chapters and is not said in this one; a bundle stays shut and unnamed. **The words the volume may not use are four and they are the same four this section may not use, and no record in this repository names them, because a document that lists the four is a document somebody can be held to; the categories are the lock.** **And the lock list is not a surname list: a capitalised search is not a search for names, and the place names are in this matter too.**

**What this phase added, and it is one thing and it is a craft method and not a fact on the page.** See the next section. Everything else in the locks is inherited and is not re-stated.
